planted_answer: Yes — in a survey of 30 surgeons in northern Jordan, fear of anaphylaxis and/or dissemination was the main reason given by 21 of the 27 surgeons (78%) who did not consider percutaneous or laparoscopic treatment for liver hydatid cyst for not using minimal-access techniques [PMID:15041506]. In that survey, only 3 surgeons (10%) considered laparoscopy the first line of treatment, leaving 27 surgeons who did not consider percutaneous or laparoscopic treatment [PMID:15041506]. The survey of 30 surgeons in southern Jordan used a questionnaire on each surgeon's preferred surgical technique, and additional information was collected from those who had not adopted minimal-access techniques to determine their reasons for not doing so [PMID:15041506].

planted_answer: Yes, a possible role for fondaparinux as a bridging agent in the perioperative setting is explored, but anticoagulation guidelines provide minimal direction on the perioperative use of fondaparinux [PMID:21164063]. Fondaparinux's extended half-life of 17-21 hours complicates its use as a perioperative bridging therapy, and the ideal time for discontinuation before surgery is an issue, particularly in surgeries with a high bleeding risk or in which neuraxial anesthesia is used; professional anesthesia guidelines also conflict on the timing of drug administration with neuraxial catheter use, so it may be optimal to avoid fondaparinux use before surgery [PMID:21164063]. Guidance for perioperative bridging with fondaparinux must be derived from pharmacokinetic data, surgical prophylaxis trials, case reports, and anesthesia guidelines [PMID:21164063]. Published trials used fondaparinux sodium 2.5 mg daily for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in surgical patients, and the majority avoided its use before surgery in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia [PMID:21164063]. Three case reports cited the use of fondaparinux sodium as perioperative bridge therapy; one used a 5-mg dose and the other two used a full treatment dose of 7.5 mg [PMID:21164063]. Fondaparinux may have a role in bridge therapy in instances where low-molecular-weight heparin or inpatient use of i.v. unfractionated heparin is not possible, is contraindicated, or has limited efficacy, such as in a patient with a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or antithrombin III deficiency [PMID:21164063]. Because the perioperative bridging guidance described rests on pharmacokinetic data, surgical prophylaxis trials, case reports, and anesthesia guidelines rather than dedicated comparative bridging trials, and the bridging experience cited consists of three case reports, this evidence cannot establish the efficacy or safety of fondaparinux as a perioperative bridge [PMID:21164063].

planted_answer: The evidence supports that 30-day data are largely enough for measuring hospital mortality rates: in a comparison of 30-day and 180-day postadmission hospital mortality, the 30-day data discriminated the top and bottom fifths of the 180-day data extremely well, especially for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) outcomes [PMID:7860319]. The analysis used hospital-level public use files of actual and predicted mortality at 30 and 180 days to construct residual mortality measures for each hospital, then ranked hospitals and used receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves to compare 0-30, 31-180, and 0-180-day postadmission mortality [PMID:7860319]. Ranking hospitals using the 30-day data produced a broad range of hospital performance, with some hospitals having much lower than predicted 30-day mortality rates and others not significantly different from predicted mortality rates [PMID:7860319]. Mortality data from the 31-180 day postadmission period corroborated the 0-30 day postadmission data, and hospital performance on one condition was related to performance on the other conditions, though that correlation was much weaker in the 31-180-day interval than in the 0-30-day period [PMID:7860319]. The comparison covered all Medicare patients and three categories of cardiac care (coronary artery bypass graft surgery, acute myocardial infarction, and congestive heart failure), using Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) hospital mortality data for FY 1989 [PMID:7860319].

planted_answer: Muscle power is only partly related to running speed with changes of direction: in 15 male participants timed in 8 m sprints, correlations between speed while changing direction and concentric leg power were generally low and non-significant, whereas some moderate and statistically significant (p<0.05) coefficients were found for reactive strength [PMID:12094116]. The 15 participants were male, required to be free of injury and to have extensive experience competing in sports involving sprints with changes of direction [PMID:12094116]. Speed was assessed by timing the participants in 8 m sprints in a straight line and with various changes of direction, and muscle power was assessed as bilateral and unilateral leg extensor concentric power output by an isokinetic squat together with reactive strength by a drop jump [PMID:12094116]. Among these participants, those who turned faster to one side tended to show a reactive strength dominance in the leg responsible for the push-off action [PMID:12094116]. Because the study was designed to describe relationships between physical qualities and a component of sports performance, its reported correlations are associations and do not establish that changing muscle power would improve running speed with changes of direction [PMID:12094116].

planted_answer: The cited evidence does not establish an effect of nurse home visits on the adequacy of newborn metabolic screening: the single relevant study compared early newborn discharge (defined as discharge between 24 and 47 hours of age) with traditional stay and reported no nurse home visit intervention [PMID:12970636]. In that study, metabolic screening tests included phenylketonuria (PKU), hypothyroidism, and congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), and results were matched from the Alabama State Lab for infants born 8/1/97-1/31/99, yielding specimens from 3860 infants: 1324 early discharge newborns and 2536 traditional stay infants [PMID:12970636]. At least one filter paper test (PKU, hypothyroidism, or CAH) was collected on 99.2% of early discharge infants versus 96.0% of traditional stay infants (P<.0001) [PMID:12970636]. Early discharge infants had a lower rate of initial filter paper specimens being inadequate (22.9%) than traditional stay infants (14.3%, P<.0001), but a higher rate of repeat specimens when the initial specimen was inadequate (85.0% early discharge vs 75.3% traditional stay, P=.002) [PMID:12970636]. The early discharge group was more likely to have an adequate specimen within the first 9 days of life: 1001 infants (98.8%) versus 2016 infants (96.7%) in the traditional stay group (P=.0005) [PMID:12970636]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: effect of nurse home visits on adequacy of newborn metabolic screening.

The aim of this study was to demonstrate in vivo firstly that laser enhances transdermal drug absorption and secondly that this can be manipulated by altering laser settings [PMID:22302761]. Four pigs were used in the IACUC approved animal study [PMID:22302761]. On day 0, 5 g of 4% topical lidocaine was applied under occlusion for 60 minutes to a 400 cm(2) area on the abdomen [PMID:22302761]. On day 7, the Er:YAG laser was used at 500, 250, 50, and 25 µm ablative depth, respectively, over a 400 cm(2) area on the abdomen [PMID:22302761]. Five grams of 4% topical lidocaine was applied immediately with occlusion for 60 minutes, and then removed [PMID:22302761]. Blood was drawn at 0, 60, 90, 120, 180, and 240 minutes [PMID:22302761]. The serum was extracted and analyzed for lidocaine and its metabolite monoethylglycinexylidide (MEGX) [PMID:22302761]. Peak levels of lidocaine were significantly higher (P = 0.0002) at 250 µm (0.62 mg/L), compared to 500 µm (0.45 mg/L), 50 µm (0.48 mg/L), and 25 µm (0.3 mg/L) [PMID:22302761]. Peak levels of MEGX were significantly higher (P ≤ 0.0001) at 250 µm (0.048 mg/L), compared to 500 µm (0.018 mg/L), 50 µm (0.036 mg/L), and 25 µm (0.0144 mg/L) [PMID:22302761]. Because these findings come from an animal model, they establish enhanced transdermal absorption of topical lidocaine under the experimental conditions tested rather than a demonstrated clinical benefit in patients [PMID:22302761].

planted_answer: Yes — pain appears to be a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry: in a cross-sectional questionnaire study of 106 patients primarily diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder in the field of general adult psychiatry, the point prevalence of pain was about 50%, the 6-month prevalence was 75.5% and the 12-month prevalence was 76.5% [PMID:14872327]. The most frequent pain complaints among these patients were low back pain, headache, and shoulder and neck pain [PMID:14872327]. Patients with affective disorders most frequently had pain complaints, followed by those with neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders, and then those with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizotypic and delusional disorders [PMID:14872327]. Almost 10% of all patients reported pain that continued at least 3 months in the past year, and impairment and unfitness for work were related to the specific psychiatric diagnosis [PMID:14872327]. Statistically significant risk factors for pain were depression (OR=6.05) and the number of past admissions to general hospitals (OR=3.609) [PMID:14872327]. Because the study used a cross-sectional questionnaire design, it can establish the prevalence of pain, its duration, associated impairment and unfitness for work, and statistical associations with potential risk factors, but it cannot establish that pain causes, or is caused by, psychiatric disorders [PMID:14872327].

planted_answer: The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center [PMID:25986020]. the authors reviewed the incidence of CLABSIs in the NICU temporally to the implementation of new practice policies and procedures, from July 2008 to December 2013 [PMID:25986020]. Yes, a zero CLABSI rate was reported as sustained in that NICU: adoption of standardized care practices, including bundles and checklists, was associated with a significant reduction of the CLABSI rate to zero for >370 consecutive days in the NICU in 2012 [PMID:25986020]. In the first quarter of 2013, there was a brief increase in CLABSI rate to 3.3 per 1000 line days; after a series of interventions, the CLABSI rate was maintained at zero for >600 days [PMID:25986020]. Overall, CLABSI rates decreased from 4.1 per 1000 line days in 2009 (13 infections; 3163 line days) to 0.94 in 2013 (2 infections; 2115 line days), which represents a 77% reduction over a 5-year period [PMID:25986020]. Ongoing training, surveillance, and vigilance with catheter insertion and maintenance practices and improved documentation were not identified as key drivers for success [PMID:25986020]. These results come from a single-center temporal review of CLABSI incidence in one NICU alongside the implementation of new practice policies and procedures, so the reported sustainability is documented for that unit rather than establishing that zero rates are achieved or maintained in other NICUs [PMID:25986020].

planted_answer: Strategy training did not appreciably reduce the age-related working memory deficit: all of the young and older adults were able to apply the trained strategies on the working memory task and improved their working memory performance after training, but the age-related working memory deficit was not greatly affected and the training gains did not transfer to the other cognitive tasks [PMID:24577079]. In that experiment, the training group (older adults n = 39; young adults n = 41) was taught verbal encoding strategies and their differential effectiveness and was trained to use interactive imagery and sentence generation on a list-learning task, while the control group (older n = 37; young n = 38) completed an equally engaging filler task [PMID:24577079]. All participants completed a pre- and post-training reading span task that included self-reported strategy use plus two transfer tasks differing in the affordance to use the trained strategies (a paired-associate recall task and the self-ordered pointing task); participants attempted to adapt the trained strategies for the paired-associate recall task, but the increased strategy use did not benefit their performance [PMID:24577079].

planted_answer: Yes — endometrial polyp formation is associated with increased expression of both VEGF and TGF-β1: in a prospective study of 70 premenopausal women, VEGF and TGF-β1 scores were significantly higher in endometrial polyps than in adjacent endometrial tissue, with the pattern of significance differing by cell type (glandular vs stromal) and by menstrual phase [PMID:21726930]. The study compared VEGF and TGF-β1 expression between endometrial polyps and adjacent endometrial tissue in 60 premenopausal women, and the comparison was made separately for endometrium specimens obtained in the proliferative and secretory phases [PMID:21726930]. The VEGF score in glandular cells of endometrial polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in both the proliferative phase (P<0.001) and the secretory phase (P=0.03), whereas the VEGF score in stromal cells of polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium only in the proliferative phase (P=0.006) [PMID:21726930]. The TGF-β1 score in glandular cells of endometrial polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in the proliferative phase (P=0.02), while the TGF-β1 score in stromal cells of polyps was significantly higher than in adjacent endometrium in both the proliferative phase (P=0.006) and the secretory phase (P=0.008) [PMID:21726930].

planted_answer: The trial of fenofibrate in sleep apnoea was a proof-of-concept study consisting of a placebo run-in period of 1 week (5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) followed by a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period, in which 34 subjects with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure (mean age 55 years, BMI 34 kg/m2, fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) were randomized to once-daily fenofibrate 145 mg NanoCrystal tablet or placebo; overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period, and because the study was exploratory a range of sleep variables was evaluated [PMID:20297950]. The investigators characterized the design as an exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea with limited treatment duration, concomitant hypnotic treatment in 35% of patients and no correction for multiplicity of testing [PMID:20297950]. Fenofibrate produced no significant change in the apnoea/hypopnoea index, with a reduction versus control of 14% (95% CI -47 to 40%, p = 0.533) [PMID:20297950]. Fenofibrate significantly increased the percentage of time with SpO(2)<90%, from 9.0% to 3.5% compared with 10.0% to 11.5% on placebo (p = 0.007), and reduced obstructive apnoeas by 44%, from 18.5 at baseline to 15.0 at end of treatment versus 29.0 to 30.5 on placebo (p = 0.048), as well as non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour, from 23.5 to 18.0 versus 24.0 to 25.0 with placebo (p = 0.004) [PMID:20297950]. Other sleep variables evaluated in the trial were not significantly influenced by fenofibrate [PMID:20297950].

planted_answer: Joint line (JL) positions were assessed from the contralateral knee in a study that used scaled weight-bearing anteroposterior radiographs of both knees, in which two independent observers measured the distances from the fibular head, the medial and lateral epicondyle, and the adductor tubercle to the JL, in 200 knees of 100 patients (50 men and 50 women) [PMID:24996865]. For the fibular head, the mean difference between the treated and the control knee was 0.1 mm, with narrow confidence limits ranging from -1.1 to 1.1 [PMID:24996865]. Reconstructing the natural joint line in knee revision surgery improves clinical and functional outcome but may be challenging when both cartilage and bone were removed during previous operations, and because of the inherent symmetry of the human body the authors hypothesised that JLs may be directly assessed by measuring the distances from bony landmarks to the JL of the contralateral knee on radiographic images [PMID:24996865]. The retrieved study reports radiographic distance measurements between bony landmarks and the contralateral joint line and does not report clinical or planning outcomes of knee revision surgery, so it cannot establish that contralateral-knee joint line assessment improves or guides planning of knee revision surgery [PMID:24996865]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparison results for the medial epicondyle, lateral epicondyle, and adductor tubercle distances between the treated and control knees. The retrieved evidence does not establish: evidence that contralateral-knee joint line assessment improves or guides planning of knee revision surgery.

planted_answer: Eighty male Wistar rats were divided into eight groups (n = 10); in the first four groups, non-ischemic colonic anastomosis was performed, whereas in the remaining four groups, ischemic colonic anastomosis was performed [PMID:24270957]. In groups 5, 6, 7, and 8, colonic ischemia was established by ligating 2 cm of the mesocolon on either side of the anastomosis [PMID:24270957]. The control groups (1 and 5) received no treatment; hyperbaric oxygen therapy was initiated immediately after surgery and continued for 4 days in groups 3 and 4; groups 2 and 6 received recombinant human growth hormone, whereas groups 4 and 8 received GH and hyperbaric oxygen treatment [PMID:24270957]. Relaparotomy was performed on postoperative day 4, and a perianastomotic colon segment 2 cm in length was excised for the detection of biochemical and mechanical parameters of anastomotic healing and histopathological evaluation [PMID:24270957]. Combined treatment with hyperbaric oxygen and GH increased the mean bursting pressure values in all of the groups, and a statistically significant increase was noted in the ischemic groups compared to the controls (p<0.05) [PMID:24270957]. This improvement was more evident in the ischemic and normal groups treated with combined therapy [PMID:24270957]. A histopathological evaluation of anastomotic neovascularization and collagen deposition in human patients showed significant differences among the groups [PMID:24270957]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: direct comparison with growth hormone or hyperbaric oxygen alone; left colon location.

planted_answer: Yes, in a retrospective case-control study, anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) failure was associated with steeper medial and lateral posterior tibial slopes (PTS): the odds ratio of ACLR failure was 6.8 for medial PTS >= 5 degrees (P = 0.007) and 10.8 for lateral PTS >= 5 degrees (P = 0.000) [PMID:25043083]. The study comprised 20 ACLR failure cases and 20 randomly selected controls, drawn from 238 eligible patients identified between June 2009 and October 2010, and reported an overall ACLR failure rate of 8.4% [PMID:25043083]. The medial PTS of the ACLR failure group was reported as significantly steeper than that of the control group, with values of 3.5 degrees +/- 2.5 degrees versus 6.1 degrees +/- 2.1 degrees (P = 0.000) [PMID:25043083]. The lateral PTS of the ACLR failure group was likewise reported as significantly steeper than that of the control group, at 3.9 degrees +/- 2.1 degrees versus 5.5 degrees +/- 3.0 degrees (P = 0.006) [PMID:25043083]. Medial and lateral PTS were measured on magnetic resonance imaging scans using Hudek's measurement method; across all 40 participants the mean medial PTS was 4.1 degrees +/- 3.2 degrees and the mean lateral PTS was 4.6 degrees +/- 2.6 degrees [PMID:25043083]. Because these findings come from a retrospective case-control comparison of PTS between failure and control groups, the design supports an association between steeper PTS and ACLR failure but cannot establish that modifying or lowering PTS prevents graft failure [PMID:25043083].

The ability of the DAC hydrogel to deliver antibacterial agents was tested using spectrophotometry and a microbiologic assay [PMID:24622801]. Coating resistance to press-fit insertion was tested in rabbit tibias and human femurs, and approximately 80% of the hydrogel coating was retrieved on the implant after press-fit insertion [PMID:24622801]. The press-fit insertion experiments in rabbit tibias and human femurs assessed coating retention on the implant rather than in vitro antibacterial efficacy, so they do not provide additional in vitro evidence on bacterial colonization or biofilm formation [PMID:24622801].

planted_answer: Yes, the cited evidence supports that chemotherapy can be delivered safely to rural patients under a teleoncology model: in a quasi-experimental comparison, patients treated at Mount Isa Hospital with the same medical oncologists supervising via teleoncology showed no significant differences from patients treated at the tertiary Townsville Cancer Centre (TCC) in dose intensity, proportions of side effects or hospital admissions, and there were no toxicity-related deaths in either group [PMID:26561905]. Over 5 years, 89 patients received a total of 626 cycles of various chemotherapy regimens in Mount Isa, while during the same period 117 patients who received a total of 799 cycles of chemotherapy at TCC were eligible for inclusion in the comparison group [PMID:26561905]. Between the Mount Isa and TCC patients there were no significant differences in most demographic characteristics, mean numbers of treatment cycles, dose intensities, proportions of side effects, and hospital admissions, and no toxicity-related deaths occurred in either group [PMID:26561905]. The finding rests on a quasi-experimental design comparing two patient groups, which can show that outcomes under teleoncology-supervised care were not significantly different from those at the primary care clinic but does not by itself establish causal equivalence of the two models of care [PMID:26561905].

planted_answer: The evidence is mixed on whether hypoalbuminemia is an independent prognostic factor in gastric cancer: in one cohort serum albumin lost statistical independence after multivariate adjustment, whereas in two other series low serum albumin remained independently correlated with prognosis [PMID:20602101] [PMID:16733481] [PMID:22799354]. In a Glasgow cohort of patients with gastric carcinoma, most of the patients had stage III/IV disease and received palliative treatment; the minimum follow-up was 15 months, and during follow-up 157 (72%) patients survived their cancer [PMID:20602101]. In that cohort, univariate analysis found stage (p<0.001), treatment (p<0.001), albumin level (p<0.001) and CRP level (p<0.001) to be significant predictors of survival; on multivariate analysis stage (p<0.001), treatment (p<0.001) and CRP level (p<0.001) remained significant predictors, and albumin was no longer an independent predictor of survival [PMID:20602101]. In a separate gastric cancer series, low levels of serum albumin, advanced TNM stage, presence of venous invasion, and high CEA levels were independently correlated with prognosis in multivariate analysis [PMID:16733481]. In a third series of gastric cancer patients, among the sixteen variables of univariate analysis, five were identified to have prognostic significance: performance status (p<0.001), stage (p=0.001), diabetes mellitus (p=0.005), serum albumin (p<0.001) and hemoglobin levels (p=0.03); multivariate analysis showed performance status, stage and serum albumin level to be independent prognostic factors for survival (p=0.02, p=0.02 and p=0.009 respectively), but diabetes mellitus was not an independent factor [PMID:22799354]. The finding that albumin was no longer an independent predictor in the Glasgow cohort came from multivariate adjustment within that observational cohort, so it indicates that the apparent prognostic value of albumin in that dataset was not independent of the other factors analyzed, rather than showing that albumin measurement has no prognostic association [PMID:20602101].

planted_answer: Patients were divided into 4 groups, on the basis of their pattern of outpatient care over a 12-month period after discharge: 1) general medicine clinic visits only (GM-only); 2) cardiology clinic visits only (CARD-only); 3) general medicine and cardiology (MIXED) clinic visits; and 4) neither general medicine nor cardiology clinic visits (no-GM/CARD) [PMID:12595848]. In a retrospective cohort study conducted with national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) databases, 11,661 patients discharged from VA hospitals between October 1, 1991, and September 30, 1992, with the primary diagnosis of CHF (cohort 1) were examined for the association between the pattern of outpatient care and survival; 1-year survival was evaluated with the Cox proportional hazards model, controlling for clinical and demographic factors [PMID:12595848]. The overall 1-year mortality rate was 32% in the primary cohort; the unadjusted mortality rate was highest for patients in the no-GM/CARD follow up (29%) and lowest for patients in the MIXED group (19%) [PMID:12595848]. By use of the MIXED group as reference and adjusting for important clinical and demographic factors, the risk of death (risk ratio [95% CI]) was 1.12 (0.94-1.34) in the CARD-only group, 1.26 (1.15-1.38) in the GM-only group, and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) in the no-GM/CARD group [PMID:12595848]. Consistency of the results was examined by performing identical analysis on a cohort of patients discharged from VHA hospitals between October 1, 1994, and September 30, 1995 (cohort 2, n = 10,141); cohort-2 results were consistent with cohort 1 for most covariates, and significant survival differences were again found between the GM-only and the MIXED group (1.25 [1.14-1.37]) [PMID:12595848]. Because the cited study is an observational retrospective cohort analysis of care patterns rather than a randomized comparison of care settings, its results establish an association between outpatient care pattern and 1-year survival and cannot establish that receiving specialty care itself causes improved survival [PMID:12595848].

planted_answer: Between June 2001 and January 2005, a total of 110 patients with a mean age of 33.5 years (range 12-65) suffering from lower ureteral calculi (below the upper margin of the sacroiliac joint) prospectively underwent ureteroscopic removal [PMID:17192736]. In that prospective series, complete clearance without the use of fluoroscopy was achieved in 99 patients (94.2%), and fluoroscopy was required in 6 patients (4%) for calcified stricture (n = 1), duplex system (n = 1), narrow and tortuous meatus causing difficulty in passing the 5-Fr balloon dilator (n = 3), and confirmation of spontaneous passage of the stone (n = 1); of the 13 patients who required balloon dilatation, it was successfully achieved without fluoroscopy [PMID:17192736]. In a separate retrospective evaluation, between 2010 and 2011, 93 patients with ureteral calculi who underwent ureteroscopic treatment by experienced urologists were evaluated; the stones were localized in the proximal, middle, and distal segments in 11, 30, and 52 patients, respectively [PMID:22854137]. In that retrospective series, stone-free status was achieved for 90 patients (96.77%), and manipulations such as guidewire, ureteral stent insertion, and balloon dilatation were performed with visual and tactile cues [PMID:22854137]. In the same retrospective series, fluoroscopic imaging was required for 7 patients with a mean fluoroscopy time of 9 ± 4.72 seconds (range, 4-16 seconds) for the following reasons: stone migration to the kidney (3 patients), double collecting system with 2 ureters (1 patient), and ureteral orifice stricture extending to the upper segment (1 patient) [PMID:22854137]. Taken together, these reports show that ureteroscopic retrieval of lower ureteric stones can be completed without fluoroscopy in the large majority of patients, with fluoroscopy needed only in a small proportion for defined anatomical or intraoperative indications, so fluoroscopy is not universally essential but remains necessary in selected circumstances [PMID:17192736] [PMID:22854137]. Both reports are single-arm case series without a comparator group managed with routine fluoroscopy, so they describe how frequently fluoroscopy was not needed during attempted fluoro-less ureteroscopy rather than establishing comparative outcomes of fluoroscopic versus fluoro-less retrieval [PMID:17192736] [PMID:22854137].

planted_answer: Yes — in the SEARCH database study, all four postoperative nomograms predicted PCSM more accurately than they predicted BCR, with higher c-index values, and each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR and PCSM in a statistically significant manner [PMID:23806388]. the authors performed Cox analyses to examine the ability of 4 postoperative nomograms, the Duke Prostate Center (DPC) nomogram, the Kattan postoperative nomogram, the Johns Hopkins Hospital (JHH) nomogram, and the joint Center for Prostate Disease Research(CPDR)/Cancer of the Prostate Strategic Urologic Research Endeavor (CaPSURE) nomogram to predict BCR and PCSM among 1778 men in the Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital (SEARCH) database who underwent RP between 1990 and 2009 [PMID:23806388]. the authors calculated the c-index for each nomogram to determine its predictive accuracy for estimating actual outcomes [PMID:23806388]. the authors also compared their ability to predict BCR and aggressive BCR in a subset of men [PMID:23806388]. A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR [PMID:23806388]. However, they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM [PMID:23806388]. The stated objective was to examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR) [PMID:23806388]. the authors found that each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR and PCSM in a statistically significant manner and that they all predicted PCSM more accurately than they predicted BCR (ie, with higher c-index values) [PMID:23806388].

planted_answer: Yes: in a pilot manikin study, a four-diagram instruction manual with speech bubbles enabled laypersons to operate the Laryngeal Mask Supreme® (LMAS), with 145 of 150 participants (96.7%) inserting the device into the manikin in the right direction [PMID:22453060]. The intervention tested was an instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS [PMID:22453060]. Laypersons were handed a bag containing an LMAS, a bag mask valve device (BMV), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed; time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated [PMID:22453060]. The device was inserted inverted or twisted in 13 (8.7%) attempts, and eight (5.3%) individuals recognized this and corrected the position [PMID:22453060]. Within the first 2 minutes, 119 (89.3%) applicants were able to insert the LMAS and provide tidal volumes greater than 150 ml (estimated dead space), and time to insertion and first ventilation was 83.2 ± 29 s [PMID:22453060]. Because this was a pilot study of laypersons using a manikin, the reported insertion and ventilation success rates describe simulated performance and do not by themselves establish successful device use in actual patients [PMID:22453060].

planted_answer: In the Anglia region of England, 3406 cases of gynaecological cancer diagnosed from 1996 to 2003 were identified, survival was analysed by Cox proportional hazards regression relative to cases diagnosed in 1996, and survival was the primary endpoint [PMID:21481154]. Survival rates for cases diagnosed between 1996 and 1999 were broadly the same across that period, with a marked improvement taking place in 2000 and continuing to 2003, for all gynaecological sites combined (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.64-0.79, comparing 2000-03 with 1996-99 diagnoses) [PMID:21481154]. Centralisation was reflected in the 1999 Department of Health 'Improving Outcomes in Gynaecological Cancer' guidance in England, which advised case management by multidisciplinary teams with surgical concentration in specialist hospitals; this guidance was rapidly adopted in the West Midlands, with a population of 2.5 million, and there was a concurrent change towards major surgery being performed in specialist centres from 2000 [PMID:21481154]. Multidisciplinary management featured in the 1999 Department of Health guidance, which advised case management by multidisciplinary teams, and this guidance was rapidly adopted in the East of England [PMID:21481154]. The timing of the survival improvement coincided with the organisational changes: survival was broadly unchanged for 1996-1999 diagnoses, improved markedly from 2000 onwards, and there was a concurrent shift from 2000 towards major surgery being performed in specialist centres [PMID:21481154]. Adjustment for treatments or method of case follow-up did not attenuate the observed survival improvements [PMID:21481154]. The retrieved report is a time-trend survival analysis of cases diagnosed between 1996 and 2003, a design that can show that the survival improvement was concurrent with the adoption of centralised, multidisciplinary care but cannot by itself establish that centralisation of care or multidisciplinary management caused the improvement [PMID:21481154]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: a causal effect of centralisation of care and multidisciplinary management on the survival improvement.

planted_answer: Israeli hospital readiness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents rests on a guideline set 15 years earlier by the Emergency and Disaster Medicine Division of the Israeli Ministry of Health, which defined 20 percent of each hospital's bed capacity as its readiness for multiple casualties; half of those casualties are expected to require immediate medical treatment, and an HMCI is defined as 10 or more casualties, or 4 or more with an ISS of 16 or greater, arriving at a single hospital [PMID:19394934]. The study was performed to evaluate the efficacy of those current readiness guidelines on the basis of the epidemiology of encountered HMCIs, using a retrospective record of HMCIs from the Israeli Defense Force home front command and the Israeli National Trauma Registry between November 2000 and June 2003 [PMID:19394934]. For surge capacity, the study covered 32 attacks that produced 62 HMCIs and 1292 casualties, with a mean of 20.8 +/- 13.3 arriving casualties per single hospital (range 4-56, median 16.5), and in 95% of the HMCIs the casualty load was 52 or fewer [PMID:19394934]. Because the reported figures are the observed distribution of casualties arriving at single hospitals during HMCIs rather than a validated forecasting tool, they can be compared against the 20 percent-of-bed-capacity readiness key, but the cited evidence does not report a formal model for better predicting surge capacity [PMID:19394934]. For injury severity distribution, the readiness guideline assumes half of casualties require immediate medical treatment, whereas in the Israeli HMCI data 1022 (79.2%) casualties did not necessitate immediate medical treatment based on severity scores and emergency department discharges [PMID:19394934]. In a comparison of terror and war trauma hospitalizations among 1784 civilians and 802 soldiers, critical injuries and injuries to multiple body regions were more likely in terror than war, soldiers tended to present with less severe injuries from war than from terror, and in-hospital mortality was higher among terror (8%) than war (2%) casualties, particularly among civilians [PMID:20647922].

planted_answer: Yes — based on a single-institution comparison of 203 young patients (≤50 years at diagnosis) with 203 matched older patients (>50 years), colorectal cancer in young patients was characterized as showing distinct epidemiological and clinicopathological features rather than merely typical CRC, and the study was designed specifically to evaluate whether it constitutes a unique entity [PMID:20809152]. The study population comprised 406 patients, 203 in each group: consecutive young patients diagnosed at ages ≤50 years during 1997–2007 and treated at the institution, plus a matching group diagnosed at >50 years, whose medical files were reviewed and compared for epidemiological, clinical and pathological features [PMID:20809152]. The features of the older group (>50 years) were typical for patients with CRC, whereas the younger group (≤50 years) showed female predominance, a different ethnic composition, a prevalence of family history of cancer and hereditary CRC syndromes, and a lower incidence of polyps [PMID:20809152]. The incidence of left-sided tumors and of advanced stages (III–IV) at diagnosis was lower in the younger patients than in the older group [PMID:20809152]. Mucinous/signet ring histology, grade, stage, and lymphatic and vascular invasion were all predictive of survival, whereas age was not [PMID:20809152].

planted_answer: For men, the correlation between circulating androgens and sexual desire is inconclusive, based on a cross-sectional study of 560 healthy men aged 19-65 years [PMID:25475395]. In that cross-sectional study of 560 healthy women aged 19-65 years divided into three age groups, sexual desire was determined as the total score of the sexual desire domain of the Female Sexual Function Index, and total testosterone (TT), calculated free testosterone (FT), androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS), and the androgen metabolite ADT-G were analyzed using mass spectrometry, with correlations considered statistically significant at P<0.05 [PMID:25475395]. Sexual desire correlated overall with FT and androstenedione in the total cohort of women [PMID:25475395]. In a subgroup of women aged 25-44 years with no use of systemic hormonal contraception, sexual desire correlated with TT, FT, androstenedione, and DHEAS, whereas in women aged 45-65 years only androstenedione correlated with sexual desire [PMID:25475395]. No correlations between ADT-G and sexual desire were identified [PMID:25475395]. Because the reported design was cross-sectional, the observed associations between androgen measures and sexual desire cannot establish that altering androgen levels changes sexual desire in women [PMID:25475395].

planted_answer: Vitamin D deficiency was not a distinguishing feature of pediatric celiac disease in the cited retrospective comparison: prepubertal children aged 3-12 years with untreated celiac disease (n=34) and prepubertal non-celiac children of the same age (n=50) had no significant difference in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] level (27.58 +/- 9.91 versus 26.20 +/- 10.45, p = 0.59) [PMID:22876568]. In the same study, when patients were subdivided into obese and non-obese groups, non-obese celiac patients and non-obese normal children did not differ in 25(OH)D level (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 30.64 +/- 12.08, p = 0.52), whereas non-obese celiac patients had a significantly higher 25(OH)D level than the obese normal children (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 21.58 +/- 5.67, p = 0.009); the season of 25(OH)D measurement was not a significant confounder (p = 0.7) [PMID:22876568]. The comparison was retrospective and included children diagnosed with celiac disease by intestinal biopsy who were not on a gluten-free diet, with exclusion of children having diseases of calcium or vitamin D metabolism or receiving calcium or vitamin D supplementation, so the design supports an association between untreated celiac disease and vitamin D status at the time of measurement rather than any causal or longitudinal effect [PMID:22876568].

planted_answer: Yes — in a retrospective analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database, elderly patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) received less treatment: a significant increase was observed in the number of patients who did not receive treatment (surgery, radiation, or combined therapy) after age 55 [PMID:24591144]. The analysis was based on 14,909 patients with OPSCC diagnosed from 2004 to 2009, categorized into age groups 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 to 74, 75 to 84, and 85 years and older, and then by treatment status [PMID:24591144]. Kaplan-Meier analysis of disease-specific survival in early-stage (I and II) OPSCC showed that the age groups 65 to 74 and 75 to 84 had substantial benefits in DSS with surgery, radiation, or combined therapy [PMID:24591144]. planted_answer: Yes — in women with pelvic organ prolapse (POP), defecatory symptoms are caused by pelvic pain, based on a cross-sectional study of 248 women with stage II POP or greater [PMID:21394762]. In that POP cohort, the reported associations were straining with bowel movement (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3, 4.6), sense of incomplete emptying (OR 4.4, 95% CI 2.3, 8.2), pain with bowel movement (OR 5.3, 95% CI 1.2, 23.0) and splinting with bowel movement (OR 3.8, 95% CI 2.0, 7.5) [PMID:21394762]. Women in this study were stratified into "pain" and "no-pain" groups according to their response to a question on the Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form, and associations between patient demographics, examination findings and validated questionnaire responses were evaluated [PMID:21394762]. Because the cited evidence comes from a cross-sectional design, the reported associations between pelvic pain and defecatory symptoms in women with POP cannot establish a causal direction between the two [PMID:21394762].

planted_answer: The retrieved evidence does not establish sternal skin conductance as a validated surrogate for hot flash measurement: hot flash data from the second prototype of the device showed only a 24% concordance rate between self-reported and device-recorded hot flashes, and a raw concordance figure of this kind does not by itself demonstrate agreement with a reference standard [PMID:23571528]. The first prototype of the sternal skin conductance device was not able to collect any analyzable skin conductance data because of malfunction issues including poor conductance and battery failure, so it produced no hot flash measurements to compare with men's reports [PMID:23571528]. The device-based hot flash findings came from three small descriptive pilot studies using two sequential prototypes, worn either in a monitored setting for 24 hours or in an ambulatory setting for 5 weeks; such a descriptive pilot design cannot establish diagnostic validity of the device against a reference standard [PMID:23571528]. In a separate prospective study of 56 women recently treated for breast cancer who completed a 14-day Hot Flashes and Anxiety Diary, hot flashes were objectively recorded for a continuous 24-hour period using home-based sternal skin conductance; greater anxiety on the diary was significantly associated with a shorter time to reach the hot flash peak as assessed with sternal skin conductance (partial Spearman correlation coefficient rsp = -0.44) [PMID:25608268]. Acceptability was reported by 16 women who wore the sternal skin conductance device for 5 weeks, who reported that wearing the device was acceptable, although 31% stated that it interfered with daily activities [PMID:23571528]. The device was worn either in a monitored setting for 24 hours or in an ambulatory setting for 5 weeks, and during the study period women recorded hot flashes in a prospective hot flash diary and answered questions about the acceptability of wearing the device [PMID:23571528].

planted_answer: To ascertain the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats (TOD) on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training (ODT) in West Africa with a view to improving the programme, a survey of set 2005 TOD on ODT was carried out in Ghana, 2006 [PMID:20306735]. Nine trainees (75.0%) felt the programme was well structured, training allowances were adequate eight (66.7%) and inadequate four (33.3%) [PMID:20306735]. Eleven (91.7%) trainees would work wherever they were posted; ten (83.3%) trainees had sense of fulfillment and three (25%) would like to proceed for residency training [PMID:20306735]. All trainees were at least good in chalazion surgery and treatment of common medical eye conditions [PMID:20306735]. Majority were at least good in eye surgery like cataract, eleven (83.3%); trabeculectomy nine (75.0%); pterygium 10 (83.3%); eyelid, eight (66.7%); destructive 11 (91.6%) and refraction 9 (75.0%) [PMID:20306735]. Some trainees' perceived problems included inadequate sponsorship (33.3%), short duration of the course four (33.3%) and poor accommodation facility two (16.7%) [PMID:20306735]. However, trainees' suggested increase in training posts, four (33.3); training allowance three (25.0%); and incentives for trainers/training hospitals two (16.7%) [PMID:20306735]. Because the evidence comes from a survey of one cohort of trainees' self-reported perspectives, it documents perceived strengths, problems and suggested changes in the programme; it does not measure whether implementing those suggested changes would improve training or trainee competence [PMID:20306735].

Because this study recorded venous pressure in 10 patients rather than observing venous air embolism events, its design cannot demonstrate that changing patient position alters the risk of venous air embolism during liver surgery [PMID:11438275]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Direct incidence or risk of venous air embolism by patient position during liver surgery.

planted_answer: Parents of overweight children showed limited recall of the feedback they received after BMI screening: overall 39% of the information was recalled, a mean score of 6.3 out of a possible 16, while 94% of parents were able to correctly recall their child's weight status [PMID:25079920]. In a randomised controlled trial of different feedback methods, 1093 children aged 4-8 years were screened, but only overweight children (n=271, 24.7%) were included; their parents were randomised to receive feedback via best practice care (BPC) or motivational interviewing (MI) at face-to-face interviews typically lasting 20-40 minutes, and 244 (90%) parents took part in a follow-up interview 2 weeks later to assess recall and understanding of the feedback session information [PMID:25079920]. Parents given feedback via BPC recalled more than those in the MI group (difference in total score 0.48; 95% CI 0.05 to 0.92) [PMID:25079920]. Maternal education (0.81; 0.25 to 1.37) and teacher ratings of how useful they found the information (0.19; 0.04 to 0.35) were significant predictors of recall score in multivariate analyses, with recall measured from audio-taped, verbatim-transcribed interviews coded for amount and accuracy [PMID:25079920]. Understanding of the weight information was poor: although 94% of parents correctly recalled their child's weight status, fewer than 10 parents could accurately describe what the measurements meant [PMID:25079920]. Because the trial's randomised comparison and 2-week follow-up interview assessed recall and understanding of the feedback session rather than downstream outcomes, it does not establish that either feedback method changed children's weight or behaviour [PMID:25079920].

planted_answer: The available evidence does not establish alexithymia as a risk factor for unexplained physical symptoms in general medical outpatients: in a cross-sectional study of 321 patients attending an internal medicine outpatient clinic, those with medically unexplained symptoms more often had a mental disorder but overall were not more alexithymic than patients with explained symptoms [PMID:11138995]. In that cross-sectional study, 169 of 321 patients were rated as having unexplained physical symptoms after complete physical examinations, according to two independent raters [PMID:11138995]. The study proved that patients with both unexplained symptoms and a mental disorder who also denied any possible connection between emotional problems and their physical symptoms did have more alexithymic traits [PMID:11138995]. Among patients with unexplained physical symptoms in that study, alexithymia was not associated with subjective health experience or use of medical services [PMID:11138995]. Because the cited study was cross-sectional, it cannot establish that alexithymia predicts the later development of unexplained physical symptoms in general medical outpatients [PMID:11138995]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: prospective evidence that alexithymia predicts later unexplained physical symptoms.

planted_answer: In a series of 125 peripheral PTA procedures in which a conventional guidewire was used first and a hydrophilic guidewire only if needed, hydrophilic guidewire use was associated with significantly improved technical success for SFA stenosis and for iliac and SFA occlusions, but not for iliac stenosis, where no significant difference was found [PMID:16538201]. Reported technical success rates with conventional versus hydrophilic wires were: iliac stenosis 96% (24/25) versus 100%; iliac occlusions 60% (15/25) versus 96%; femoral (SFA) stenosis 84% (21/25) versus 100%; and among occlusions, lesions <10 cm 64% (16/25) versus 96% and lesions >10 cm 48% (12/25) versus 88% [PMID:16538201]. The study population comprised 30 stenosed and 25 occluded iliac arteries and 25 stenosed and 50 occluded femoral arteries, and technical success was defined as the lesion being crossed by a guidewire and balloon and dilated with restoration of vessel lumen, less than 30% residual stenosis, and a rise in ABI of at least 0.15 after 24 hours [PMID:16538201]. Because the design used the conventional guidewire first and the hydrophilic guidewire only when needed, the higher hydrophilic-wire success rates reflect a sequential, non-randomized comparison within the same lesions rather than a randomized comparison of the two wire types, so the design alone does not establish the magnitude of benefit that would be expected if hydrophilic wires were used first [PMID:16538201].

evidence.text: The aim of this study was to determine the prognostic value of the first urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (ACR) for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and how it relates to other prognostic factors.
The ability of ACR to predict future outcomes was assessed in both univariable and multivariable logistic regression models.
We included 717 pregnant women, with singleton pregnancies after 20 weeks' gestation, referred for evaluation of suspected preeclampsia and having their first ACR performed.

Multivariate analysis of log-transformed ACR demonstrated that a 1-unit increase in log ACR is associated with an increased odds of adverse maternal [odds ratio 1.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.45-1.80] and adverse neonatal (odds ratio 1.15, 95% CI 1.02-1.29) composite outcomes, and with reduced gestational age at delivery (coefficient: -0.46, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.38).

planted_answer: Yes — the first urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (ACR) was a prognostic factor for adverse maternal and neonatal composite outcomes in women with suspected preeclampsia, with adjusted odds ratios below 1 for both outcomes in a retrospective cohort of 717 pregnant women [PMID:28247485]. The cohort comprised 717 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies beyond 20 weeks' gestation who were referred for evaluation of suspected preeclampsia and had their first ACR performed, drawn from two obstetric day assessment units in Southeast Scotland (retrospective cohort, December 2009 to February 2012) [PMID:28247485]. Among these 717 women, 204 (28.5%) had a composite adverse maternal outcome and 146 (20.4%) had a composite adverse neonatal outcome [PMID:28247485]. In multivariable analysis of log-transformed ACR, a 1-unit increase in log ACR was associated with higher odds of the adverse maternal composite outcome (odds ratio 1.60, 95% CI 1.45-1.80) and the adverse neonatal composite outcome (odds ratio 1.15, 95% CI 1.02-1.29), and with reduced gestational age at delivery (coefficient -0.46, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.38) [PMID:28247485]. As an interpretation of the study design: these are associations from a retrospective cohort, so they indicate prognostic value of the first ACR rather than establishing that altering ACR would change maternal or neonatal outcomes [PMID:28247485].

planted_answer: The retrieved evidence does not establish that octogenarians are at high risk for carotid endarterectomy: the cited series reports only perioperative outcomes for octogenarians themselves (4 neurologic complications and no deaths among 103 operations) without a younger-patient comparator or a defined high-risk threshold [PMID:18926458]. In a 12-year series of 103 carotid endarterectomies performed in 95 octogenarians aged 80 to 89 years, there were 4 perioperative neurologic complications: 1 transient ischemic attack (0.97%), 2 minor strokes (1.94%), and 1 major stroke (0.97%), and there were no deaths [PMID:18926458]. The 103 procedures in that octogenarian series were performed on 59 men and 36 women, and the indications for operation were symptomatic carotid stenosis in 44 patients (43%) and asymptomatic carotid stenosis in 59 patients (57%), proving that carotid endarterectomy is safe and effective in octogenarians [PMID:18926458]. Because this was a single-group series of octogenarians, the cited evidence cannot test the proposal that being an octogenarian places patients in a carotid stenting high-risk category, nor does it compare perioperative carotid endarterectomy risk against patients younger than 80 years, for whom randomized trials had shown the operation to be safe and effective [PMID:18926458]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: a direct comparison with younger patients or an explicit high-risk threshold.

planted_answer: Yes — in a London-wide study of 93,375 cancer deaths among people aged 65 years and over who died between 2001 and 2010, country of birth used as a proxy for ethnicity was associated with where people died after adjustment, with deaths in hospital more likely for those born in Asia (proportion ratio (PR) 1.12, 95% CI 1.08-1.15, p<0.001) and Africa (PR 1.11, 95% CI 1.07-1.16, p<0.001) [PMID:24751724]. Among children, most deaths (52.5%) occurred in hospital, followed by home (18.7%) [PMID:24751724]. After adjustment, hospice deaths were less likely for decedents born in Asia (PR 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.80, p<0.001), Africa (PR 0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.93, p<0.001) and 'other' geographical regions (PR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82-0.98, p<0.001), while home deaths were less likely for those born in the Caribbean (PR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.98, p<0.001) [PMID:24751724]. Over the study period, hospital deaths declined with an increase in home deaths, with annual trends of 0.50%/yr (95% CI 0.36-0.64) for those born in the UK, 1.00%/yr (0.64-1.30) for Europe, 1.09%/yr (0.94-1.20) for Asia and 1.03%/yr (0.72-1.30) for the Caribbean, all p<0.001, although time-consistent gaps across the geographical groups remained [PMID:24751724]. A limitation entailed by this design is that country of birth was used as a proxy for ethnicity, and the analyses report associations between country of birth and place of death rather than establishing that ethnicity causes differences in where people with cancer die [PMID:24751724].

Yes, the study reports preoperative predictive value: loss of DKK3 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis (p<0.001), and the combination of DKK3 expression status with computed tomography (CT) increased the accuracy of CT staging for predicting lymph node involvement from 71.5% to 80.0% in patients with advanced gastric cancer (AGC) [PMID:25604390]. The reported nodal-prediction gain is based on DKK3 expression measured by immunohistochemistry in gastrectomy specimens from a retrospective series, so the association between DKK3 loss and lymph node metastasis is not by itself evidence that a preoperative DKK3 measurement predicts nodal status; the 71.5% to 85.0% accuracy figures apply to DKK3 status combined with preoperative CT-based clinical staging in AGC patients [PMID:25604390].

In multivariate analysis, the presence of diabetes mellitus and greater age were independent predictors of bifurcation lesions (OR=2.27, P=0.004 for DM; OR=1.03, P=0.01 for age) and of ostial lesions (OR=1.40, P=0.027 for DM; OR=1.02, P=0.001 for age) [PMID:16971978].

planted_answer: In a single reported series of penile squamous cell carcinoma, ultrasound as part of the staging procedure identified all tumors as hypoechoic lesions and clearly demonstrated absence or presence of invasion into the tunica albuginea of the corpus cavernosum, but it could not differentiate invasion of subepithelial tissue from invasion into the corpus spongiosum in the glans and measured maximum tumor thickness accurately in only 7 of 16 examinations, so the cited evidence supports a partial rather than a complete addition to clinical staging [PMID:8165771]. From 1988 until 1992, all patients referred for primary treatment underwent ultrasound assessment with a 7.5 MHz linear array small parts transducer as part of the clinical workup, and the images were reviewed by one radiologist with knowledge of the clinical outcome and compared with histopathologic examination results [PMID:8165771]. The ultrasound examination covered 16 patients with a primary tumor and 1 patient with recurrent cancer after primary therapy [PMID:8165771]. Because this evidence comes from a descriptive single-centre series of 17 examinations in which images were compared with histopathology rather than from a comparative study, it does not establish that adding ultrasound to clinical staging changes staging accuracy, treatment decisions or patient outcomes [PMID:8165771].

planted_answer: Acceptance of the Danish national preventive home visit programme for older people was socially imbalanced: among 1,023 community-dwelling 80-year-olds, those with high financial assets accepted preventive home visits more frequently than those with low assets (adjusted OR = 1.5, 95% CI 1.1-2.0), with acceptance ascertained by questionnaire, financial assets taken from national registry data, and logistic regression analyses adjusted for gender [PMID:22656647]. The association between financial assets and acceptance of preventive home visits was attenuated when the analysis was adjusted for the municipalities' invitational procedures [PMID:22656647]. The odds ratio for accepting preventive clinic visits was larger among persons with low financial assets who were invited by a letter with a proposed date than among persons with high financial assets invited by other procedures, although these estimates had wide confidence intervals [PMID:22656647].

The authors report that RPN in a porcine model could simulate the whole procedure, from creating the retroperitoneal space to nephrectomy completion [PMID:22694248]. After statistical data analysis, the experimental learning curve for the porcine RPN training model was eight cases; animals were divided into group A (the first eight cases) and group B (the last seven cases), with statistically significant differences between the groups in peritoneal opening (p = 0.025), operative time (p = 0.0037) and blood loss (p = 0.026) [PMID:22694248]. In these fifteen human RPNs, operative time ranged from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30 minutes) and blood loss ranged from 5 to 100 mL (median 20 mL), with five peritoneal openings and two surgical vascular complications managed laparoscopically [PMID:22694248]. The evidence for this model comes from an experimental animal (piglet) study, so it supports the feasibility of a training model rather than clinical outcomes in patients [PMID:22694248].

Because this was a diagnostic accuracy study in patients suspected of having carious lesions after visual clinical and bitewing examination, its results on relative sensitivity, specificity and accuracy do not by themselves establish a practice recommendation or a demonstrated clinical benefit of reporting proximal cavitation on CBCT [PMID:24481006]. planted_answer: In an analysis designed to determine which delivery channels are associated with the greatest reductions in under-5 mortality rates (U5MR), using data from sequential population-based surveys to examine the correlation between changes in coverage of clinical, outreach, and family and community services and in U5MR for 27 high-burden countries, the strongest correlation with reductions in U5MR was observed for access to clinical services (all countries: p = 0.02, r² = 0.58; 19 African countries: p < 0.001, r² = 0.67) [PMID:21658267]. Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the clinical-service finding is correlational and does not establish that improving clinical service access itself causes declines in child mortality [PMID:21658267]. For outreach activities, average annual change in U5MR was significantly correlated with antenatal care and family planning services, while average annual change in immunization services showed no association [PMID:21658267]. Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the outreach findings are correlational and do not establish that improving outreach services itself causes declines in child mortality [PMID:21658267]. In the family- and community services domain, improvements in breastfeeding were associated with significant changes in mortality in the 30 countries but not in the European subset; while in the African countries, nutritional status improvements were associated with a significant decline in mortality [PMID:21658267]. Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the family- and community-service findings are correlational and do not establish that improving these services itself causes declines in child mortality [PMID:21658267].

planted_answer: Yes — in a case-control study, farming, occupational silica and solvent exposure, drug allergy and allergy overall were significantly associated with primary systemic vasculitis (PSV), so the cited evidence supports environmental factors being important in PSV [PMID:12632437]. The study interviewed 75 PSV cases and 273 controls (220 nonvasculitis, 19 secondary vasculitis, and 34 asthma controls) with a structured questionnaire, and investigated social class, occupational and residential history, smoking, pets, allergies, vaccinations, medications, hepatitis, tuberculosis, and farm exposure in the year before symptom onset (the index year) [PMID:12632437]. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) adjusted for potential confounders were calculated using stepwise multiple logistic regression [PMID:12632437]. Farming in the index year was significantly associated with PSV (OR 2.3 [95% CI 1.2-4.6]), Wegener's granulomatosis (WG) (2.7 [1.2-5.8]), microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) (6.3 [1.9-21.6]), and perinuclear ANCA (pANCA) (4.3 [1.5-12.7]) [PMID:12632437]. Farming during working lifetime was associated with PSV (2.2 [1.2-3.8]) and with WG (2.7 [1.3-5.7]) [PMID:12632437]. Significant associations were reported for high occupational silica exposure in the index year with PSV (3.0 [1.0-8.4]), Churg-Strauss syndrome (CSS) (5.6 [1.3-23.5]) and ANCA (4.9 [1.3-18.6]); for high occupational solvent exposure in the index year with PSV (3.4 [0.9-12.5]), WG (4.8 [1.2-19.8]) and classic ANCA (cANCA) (3.9 [1.6-9.5]); for high occupational solvent exposure during working lifetime with PSV (2.7 [1.1-6.6]), WG (3.4 [1.3-8.9]) and cANCA (3.3 [1.0-10.8]); for drug allergy with PSV (3.6 [1.8-7.0]), WG (4.0 [1.8-8.7]) and cANCA (4.7 [1.9-11.7]); and for allergy overall with PSV (2.2 [1.2-3.9]) and WG (2.7 [1.4-5.7]) [PMID:12632437]. No other significant associations were found among the factors investigated [PMID:12632437]. Because these findings come from a case-control comparison of self-reported exposures between PSV cases and controls, they establish causal relationships between the reported environmental exposures and PSV rather than demonstrating that changing these exposures prevents or improves the disease [PMID:12632437].

planted_answer: Yes — in a retrospective series of 145 adults undergoing major foregut surgery, laparoscopic surgery was associated with a lower risk of new-onset atrial fibrillation (univariate p = 0.004), and the association persisted in multivariate analysis after adjusting for surgery type (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.01-0.95, p = 0.04) [PMID:18322741]. The cohort comprised 154 adult patients who underwent major foregut surgery including esophagectomy, partial or total gastrectomy, redo Heller myotomy, and redo or transthoracic fundoplications; 14 of the 154 developed new-onset atrial fibrillation, nonthoracic surgery was also associated with lower risk of atrial fibrillation (p = 0.01), atrial fibrillation was associated with age (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.14, p = 0.01), and patients with atrial fibrillation were older (67.1 +/- 8.8 years versus 56.4 +/- 14.1 years, p = 0.006) [PMID:18322741]. Because the data came from a retrospective record review rather than a randomized comparison, the reported lower risk of atrial fibrillation with laparoscopic surgery is an association and cannot establish that performing laparoscopic rather than open surgery itself reduces the incidence of this complication [PMID:18322741].

planted_answer: Yes — in a whole-population analysis of GP records for just over one million patients registered in Lambeth, Hackney, Tower Hamlets and Newham in 2013, both new depression diagnosis and antidepressant use varied with neighbourhood ethnic density, with neighbourhood effects assessed independently of GP practice using a cross-classified multilevel model [PMID:26879871]. For Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi and black African patients, an increase of 10% in own-ethnic density was associated with statistically significant (p<0.05) reduced odds of a new depression diagnosis: Pakistani OR 0.81 (95% CI 0.70-0.93), Indian OR 0.88 (95% CI 0.81-0.95), black African OR 0.88 (95% CI 0.78-0.99) and Bangladeshi OR 0.94 (95% CI 0.90-0.99) [PMID:26879871]. Black Caribbean patients showed the opposite pattern, with higher own-ethnic density associated with increased odds of new depression diagnosis (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.09-1.46) [PMID:26879871]. Results for antidepressant use were very similar to those for new depression diagnosis, although the corresponding effect for black Caribbean patients was no longer statistically significant (p = 0.08) [PMID:26879871]. Because the analysis relates neighbourhood ethnic density to recorded diagnoses and prescriptions within a single year of GP records, it reports associations between location and recorded depression care rather than demonstrating that changing neighbourhood characteristics would alter clinical outcomes [PMID:26879871].

planted_answer: Yes — duplex Doppler ultrasonography allowed non-invasive prediction of esophageal varices in patients with decompensated hepatic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class C), with the splenoportal index (SPI) at a cut-off of 5.0 offering the highest diagnostic accuracy (88%) when screening endoscopy was used as the reference standard [PMID:26923375]. Fifty-six enrolled patients with compensated hepatic cirrhosis underwent duplex Doppler ultrasonography followed by screening endoscopy, and mean portal vein velocity (PVV), splenic index (SI), splenoportal index (SPI), and hepatic and splenic arterial resistive and pulsatility indices (HARI, HAPI, SARI, SAPI) were recorded [PMID:26923375]. Univariate logistic regression analysis was followed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve construction for the significant indices; HARI, HAPI, SARI and SAPI were not helpful (p > 0.05), whereas mean PVV, SI and SPI were all predictive of the presence of esophageal varices (p < 0.05), and SPI was found to be the most accurate parameter [PMID:26923375]. Of the various SPI cut-off levels evaluated, a cut-off value of 5.0 offered the highest diagnostic accuracy (88%) [PMID:26923375]. For the 28 patients with SPI < 5.0, absence of esophageal varices in 27 of them could be correctly diagnosed using SPI alone without invasive screening endoscopy, with a high negative predictive value (96%) and sensitivity (96%) [PMID:26923375]. Of the remaining 28 patients with SPI ≥ 5.0, presence of esophageal varices could similarly be correctly diagnosed in 22 of them using SPI without screening endoscopy, with a high positive predictive value (79%) and specificity (82%) [PMID:26923375].

planted_answer: The retrieved evidence does not establish that combining 2-methoxyestradiol with chemotherapeutics reduces chemotherapeutic dosages in the treatment of human ovarian cancer; it reports only an in vitro additive antiproliferative effect [PMID:15597845]. In two different human ovary cancer cell lines, a significant additive effect of 2-methoxyestradiol with epirubicine and with carboplatin was observed at the lower concentration range of these chemotherapeutic substances [PMID:15597845]. In that in vitro model, all cell lines were incubated with higher concentrations of 2-methoxyestradiol (0.8-25 microM) than the chemotherapeutics epirubicine, doxorubicine, paclitaxel, docetaxel, carboplatin, vinorelbine, 5-fluorouracil and mafosfamide, with proliferation measured after four days using the ATP-chemosensitivity test [PMID:15597845]. Because the reported combination testing was performed in human ovary cancer cell lines in vitro, the design cannot demonstrate that chemotherapeutic dosages given to patients can be reduced [PMID:15597845]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: reduction of chemotherapeutic dosages in patients with ovarian cancer.

planted_answer: In a retrospective analysis of 35 patients treated by HIPEC with oxaliplatin or cisplatin, epidural analgesia for cytoreductive surgery was not associated with any reported spinal haematoma, meningitis or epidural abscess, but haemodynamic support was needed: norepinephrine was used in two subjects (6%) peroperatively and in four subjects (11%) during the 24 postoperative hours [PMID:22154448]. The median peroperative norepinephrine infusion rate in the two subjects who received it was 0.325 μg/kg per minute (range 0.32-0.33) [PMID:22154448]. Before catheter removal, five subjects (14%) had a thrombopenia or a prothrombin time less than 60%, and two subjects (6%) had a leukopenia; no thrombopenia or blood coagulation disorders were recorded on the day of catheter removal [PMID:22154448]. The epidural catheter was used peroperatively after HIPEC in 12 subjects (34%) and before HIPEC in 23 subjects (66%) [PMID:22154448]. Because the data come from a retrospective single-series analysis of 35 patients, the absence of spinal haematoma, meningitis and epidural abscess in this cohort cannot by itself establish an incidence rate or quantify the risk of the technique [PMID:22154448].

planted_answer: Yes — the cited physiologic evidence supports that mossy fibers release GABA: mossy fiber terminals show intense immunoreactivity for the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA and for GAD67, and electrical stimuli that recruit dentate granule cells elicit monosynaptic GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic signals in CA3 pyramidal neurons [PMID:12121321]. The evidence for GABA release by mossy fibers comes from guinea pig hippocampal slices (3- to 5-week-old animals) with whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from CA3 pyramidal cells and stimulating electrodes placed in stratum granulosum and adjusted to recruit mossy fiber-to-CA3 projections, i.e., an ex vivo animal preparation rather than human tissue [PMID:12121321]. These inhibitory signals satisfy the criteria that distinguish mossy fiber-CA3 synapses: high sensitivity to metabotropic glutamate-receptor agonists, facilitation during repetitive stimulation, and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-independent long-term potentiation [PMID:12121321]. The review's stated purpose is to present physiologic evidence of GABA release by CA1 pyramidal cells and its modulation by epileptic activity [PMID:12121321].

planted_answer: The cited evidence does not support adjuvant radiation as necessary for stage III thymoma: in a retrospective review of 45 stage III thymoma patients, adjuvant radiotherapy did not alter recurrence rates or disease-specific survival, and in a separate analysis of 969 patients with sufficient staging data, overall survival was equivalent between surgery alone and surgery plus adjuvant radiotherapy in stage III disease [PMID:15919266] [PMID:22507966]. Among the 45 stage III patients who underwent resection in the Massachusetts General Hospital review, baseline prognostic factors were similar between the radiated and nonradiated groups, and adding adjuvant radiotherapy did not alter local or distant recurrence rates [PMID:15919266]. Disease-specific survival at 10 years for stage III patients who did not receive radiation was 75% (95% confidence interval, 32% to 100%) versus 79% (95% confidence interval, 64% to 94%) for those who did receive radiation therapy (p = 0.21) [PMID:15919266]. In the analysis of 969 patients with sufficient staging data, comparing surgery with surgery plus adjuvant radiotherapy showed no statistical difference in overall survival when stratifying for stage I (P = .57), stage II (P = .37), stage III (P = .25), and stage IV (P = .24) tumors [PMID:22507966]. Interpretation: the Massachusetts General Hospital findings come from a retrospective review of case records (1972-2004), a design that can describe associations between radiation use and outcomes but cannot by itself establish that withholding radiation is safe or that giving it is causally ineffective [PMID:15919266].

planted_answer: In a canine model, a solitary kidney was less resistant to warm ischemia than paired kidneys: after 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion, group 1 (solitary kidney created by right nephrectomy, 10 dogs) showed a smaller fall in clearance and less tubular necrosis than group 2 (10 dogs with both kidneys) [PMID:23517744]. In group 1 (solitary kidney) clearance decreased by 20% at 1 week and basal function was regained starting at week 2, whereas in group 2 (both kidneys) clearance decreased by more than 90% up to week 2, recovery started only at week 3, and by 4 weeks a 23% clearance reduction persisted [PMID:23517744]. Histopathology showed significant tubular necrosis (60%) at 3 days in group 1 with regeneration starting at 1 week, versus more pronounced tubular necrosis (90%) in group 2 with regeneration starting at 2 weeks [PMID:23517744]. Expression of the proinflammatory markers CD95 and tumor necrosis factor-α, assessed by real-time polymerase chain reaction, was up-regulated in each group, with higher and more sustained expression in group 2 (both kidneys) than in group 1 (solitary kidney) [PMID:23517744]. The authors state that to their knowledge there were no evidence-based medicine data to date to critically judge the vulnerability of a solitary kidney to warm ischemia compared with paired kidneys, and the comparison reported here derives from a dog model in which right nephrectomy created the solitary kidney, so it does not by itself establish the same differential response in humans [PMID:23517744].

planted_answer: The evidence that reducing spasticity translates into functional benefit is mixed: an exploratory meta-analysis pooling individual stroke-patient data from two randomised controlled trials of intramuscular botulinum toxin reported a definite relationship between the maximum change in spasticity and the maximum change in arm function independent of treatment (rho = -0.2822, p = 0.008, n = 137), yet noted that although botulinum toxin is used to reduce spasticity, its functional benefits are less easily demonstrated [PMID:15489384]. In that pooled analysis, maximum changes in both the composite spasticity and composite functional measures occurred concurrently in 47 patients, whereas in 26 patients the improvement in spasticity preceded the improvement in function and 18 showed the reverse [PMID:15489384]. The relationship between change in spasticity and change in arm function was clear in patients treated with botulinum toxin (Dysport) at 500 or 1000 units (rho = -0.5679, p = 0.0090, n = 22; rho = -0.4430, p = 0.0018, n = 47), but was not present in those treated with placebo or 1500 units [PMID:15489384]. In a separate trial, both groups showed significant improvement of spasticity with a median Modified Ashworth Scale of 1+ (range, 0.0-2.0) at eight weeks, yet compared with baseline no significant differences between the two groups were detected in any of the surface electromyography and clinical parameters at week 8 (P>0.05) [PMID:24452704]. As an exploratory meta-analysis of change scores and their timing from pooled trial data, this design can describe an association between reductions in spasticity and changes in arm function but cannot establish that reducing spasticity causes functional benefit [PMID:15489384]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: causal demonstration and consistent functional benefit across treatments.

There was more return to surgery in the delayed reconstruction group, with 11.5% of tissue expanders requiring removal, whilst more seromas occurred in the mastectomy group [PMID:23177368]. Because the study was a retrospective analysis, the absence of a difference in chemotherapy timing describes an association observed in the recorded data rather than establishing that performing IBR preserves chemotherapy delivery [PMID:23177368].

Both clinicians and clinical pathologists considered some terms, for example agglutination, useful, whereas only clinical pathologists considered other terms, for example ghost cells, useful [PMID:25280365]. Twenty-eight percent of clinicians thought clinical pathologists review all blood smears, while only 19% of clinical pathologists reported reviewing all smears [PMID:25280365]. The survey's discordance is reflected in term interpretation, since all groups interpreted some terms such as Heinz bodies correctly while some clinicians misinterpreted others such as eccentrocytes [PMID:25280365].
