planted_answer: In a retrospective multicenter study of 12 patients with spinal cord sarcoidosis accompanied by compressive cervical myelopathy who underwent decompressive surgery, the procedure showed limited effectiveness: postoperative recovery rates in the surgery group were -7.4% at 1 week and -1.1% at 4 weeks, and the recovery rate of the Japanese Orthopedic Association score, which increased after steroid therapy, was lower in the surgery group (18.6%) than in the nonsurgery group (62.5%), with a significant difference (P<0.01) [PMID:20736887]. Only 5 cases showed clinical improvement, and the condition of these 5 patients had worsened again at an average of 7.4 weeks after surgery [PMID:20736887]. A total of 12 patients (0.08% of cervical myelopathy) were identified from the Nagoya Spine Group database as having spinal cord sarcoidosis treated with decompressive surgery; the Nagoya Spine Group database included 1560 cases with cervical myelopathy treated with cervical laminectomy or laminoplasty from 2001 to 2005 [PMID:20736887]. As control subjects, 8 patients with spinal cord sarcoidosis without a compressive lesion who underwent high-dose steroid therapy without surgery were recruited [PMID:20736887]. Postoperative oral steroid therapy was initiated at an average of 6.4 weeks, and the average initial dose was 51.3 mg in the surgery group, while it was 54.0 mg in the nonsurgery group [PMID:20736887]. The study design was a retrospective multicenter case series with a separately recruited nonsurgical control group, so the comparison of groups cannot establish that decompressive surgery itself causes worse neurological recovery [PMID:20736887].

planted_answer: In a prospective study of 97 patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and 65 with Crohn's disease (CD) in clinical remission, calprotectin testing was assessed for its role in predicting clinical relapse, with the cutoff set at 130 mg/kg of feces and patients followed for 1 year after the test or until relapse [PMID:18802997]. Among the UC patients, the calprotectin test was positive in 44 and 26 of them relapsed within a year, whereas 11 of the 53 UC patients with a negative test relapsed within the same time frame; a significant correlation emerged between a negative calprotectin test and the probability of relapse in UC patients (P= 0.000) [PMID:18802997]. Among the CD patients, 30 had a positive calprotectin test and 13 of them relapsed within a year, as did 7 of the 35 with a negative test result; only cases of colonic CD showed a significant correlation between a positive calprotectin test and the probability of relapse, with 6 colonic CD patients positive for the test and 4 relapsing (P= 0.02) [PMID:18802997]. The reported evidence for calprotectin as a relapse marker in this prospective remission cohort consists of correlations between test positivity and relapse probability within 1 year, so the design as reported does not establish that acting on calprotectin results alters clinical outcomes [PMID:18802997].

planted_answer: The single retrieved study of this question reviewed medical records of all blunt trauma patients admitted to the trauma service from January 1, 1992, to March 31, 1998 [PMID:10798511]. Physical examination for the detection of abdominal injuries has been considered unreliable in alcohol-intoxicated trauma patients, and computed tomography (CT) has been described as playing the primary role in these abdominal evaluations [PMID:10798511]. The patients studied had a blood alcohol level of at least 80 mg/dL, a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15, and an unremarkable abdominal examination [PMID:10798511]. Of 324 patients studied, 317 (97%) had CT scans negative for abdominal injury [PMID:10798511]. Abdominal injuries were identified in 7 patients (2%), with only 2 (0.6%) requiring abdominal exploration [PMID:10798511]. A significant association was found between major chest injury and abdominal injury [PMID:10798511]. Because these data come from a retrospective medical record review of patients who underwent CT, the findings describe the yield of abdominal CT in this intoxicated population but do not compare a selective-CT or no-CT strategy against universal scanning, so they do not establish that omitting or limiting abdominal CT in such patients is safe or misses no clinically significant injuries [PMID:10798511]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Safety and missed-injury rate of selective or no abdominal CT.

In-vitro experiments in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and rat macrophages showed that leptin induced NADPH oxidase activation [PMID:20577124]. Inhibition of the leptin-induced NADPH oxidase activity by wortmannin and bisindolyl maleimide suggested a direct involvement of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase and protein kinase C pathways, respectively [PMID:20577124]. Leptin-induced NADPH oxidase activation promoted macrophage proliferation [PMID:20577124]. planted_answer: Yes — in the longitudinal study of 500 men (250 sons of men with a lifetime history of substance use disorder, the High Average Risk group, and 250 sons of men with no such history, the Low Average Risk group), the Transmissible Liability Index measured at ages 10-12 in late childhood was significantly associated with the number and severity of lifetime suicide attempts [PMID:25699562]. The Transmissible Liability Index was delineated at baseline (age 10-12) and age-specific versions were administered at 12-14, 17, 19, 22, and 25 years of age, covering suicidal behavior from preadolescence (12-14) through young adulthood (25) [PMID:25699562].

planted_answer: Socioeconomic status did matter for quality of life in newly diagnosed breast cancer patients at baseline, but not at the three-month follow-up assessment: lower-status patients reported more health problems, less functioning and more symptoms than affluent patients initially, yet at follow-up there was no significant difference between the groups and no consistent pattern emerged [PMID:12846929]. In this prospective study, 129 lung cancer patients entered, and complete data at both baseline and follow-up were available for 82 patients; 57% of patients were of lower socioeconomic status, and these patients had more health problems, less functioning and more symptoms compared with affluent patients. Socioeconomic status was derived for each patient using the Carstairs and Morris Deprivation Category ranging from 1 (least deprived) to 7 (most deprived) on the basis of the postcode sector of their address [PMID:12846929]. At baseline, the differences between socioeconomic groups were statistically significant for physical mobility (P = 0.05), energy (P = 0.01), role functioning (P = 0.04), physical functioning (P = 0.03) and breathlessness (P = 0.02); quality of life was measured with the Nottingham Health Profile, the EORTC QLQ-C30 and its lung cancer supplement QLQ-LC13 at baseline and three months after initial treatment [PMID:12846929]. At the follow-up assessment three months after initial treatment, there was no significant difference in quality of life between the socioeconomic patient groups, nor did any consistent pattern emerge [PMID:12846929].

planted_answer: In a qualitative study nested in a larger six-country mixed-method project examining two English-language MPH programs (a distance program offered from South Africa and a residential program in the Netherlands) that train students from a diversity of countries, in-depth interviews with 10 graduates per program working in low- and middle-income health systems, together with their peers and supervisors, found that impact on the workplace was reported as considerable, including changes in management and leadership: many participants reported promotion to a leadership position as well as expanded or revitalized management roles [PMID:27549226]. The development of leadership capacity was highly valued among many graduates, and this capacity was cited by a number of supervisors and peers [PMID:27549226]. Because the findings rest on self-reported accounts from a small purposive qualitative sample, the authors note that self-selection of graduates and their role in selecting peers and supervisors may have resulted in some bias, some graduates could not be traced, and social acceptability bias may have influenced findings, so the reported leadership and management impact cannot be read as an unbiased measured effect [PMID:27549226]. Wider impact in the workplace took the form of introducing workplace innovations such as setting up an AIDS and addiction research center and research involvement, while teaching and training, advocacy, and community engagement were other ways in which medical students' influence reached a wider target grouping [PMID:27549226]. Beyond the workplace, graduates were reported to use an intersectoral approach and to achieve national reach through policy advisory roles to Ministries of Health, policy development, and capacity building [PMID:27549226]. Work conditions and context influenced how conducive the setting was for innovation and the extent to which graduates were able to have an effect [PMID:27549226].

planted_answer: HFNC were not noisier than bubble CPAP in preterm infants: there was no evidence of a difference in average noise levels measured at the external auditory meatus, with a mean difference (95% CI) of -1.6 (-4.0 to 0.9) dBA for HFNC compared to BCPAP [PMID:24625433]. At low frequency (500 Hz), HFNC was mean (95% CI) 3.0 (0.3 to 5.7) dBA quieter than BCPAP, proving that HFNC is always quieter [PMID:24625433]. These findings come from an observational study of preterm infants receiving HFNC or BCPAP in which noise within the external auditory meatus was measured with a microphone probe tube connected to a calibrated digital dosimeter across a range of frequencies and reported as dBA; 21 HFNC and 13 BCPAP noise measurements were performed in 21 infants, with HFNC gas flows of 2-5 L/min and BCPAP gas flows of 6-10 L/min at set pressures of 5-7 cm of water [PMID:24625433].

planted_answer: Yes — in winter oil-seed rape (Brassica napus subsp. oleifera), pectins are implicated in cold acclimation: in leaves of two double-haploid lines differing in winter survival and blackleg (Leptosphaeria maculans) resistance, acclimation at 2 degrees C promoted leaf expansion while freezing resistance developed, and these effects were associated with increases in leaf tensile stiffness, cell wall and pectin contents, pectin methylesterase (EC 3.1.1.11) activity and low-methylated pectin content, independently of genotype [PMID:18222909]. The cold-induced modifications in cell wall properties were more pronounced in the leaves of the more pathogen-resistant genotype [PMID:18222909]. Pectins are also implicated in de-acclimation of winter oil-seed rape: de-acclimation promoted leaf expansion and reversed most of the cold-induced effects, with the exception of pectin methylesterase activity, which remained altered [PMID:18222909].

planted_answer: In a single-institution series of 49 epithelial ovarian cancer patients (median age 57 years, range 28-76) undergoing quaternary cytoreduction for relapse a median of 16 months (range 2-142 months) after previous chemotherapy, the median duration of surgery was 292 min [PMID:23321509]. Major operative morbidity after quaternary cytoreduction was 18.6% and 30-day mortality was 2%; mean overall survival was 23.05 months (95% CI 15.5-30.6) over a mean follow-up of 18.41 months (95% CI 12.64-24.18) [PMID:23321509]. The study was designed to evaluate surgical outcome and survival benefit after quaternary cytoreduction in epithelial ovarian cancer relapse, and it systematically evaluated all consecutive patients undergoing quaternary cytoreduction at one institution over a 12-year period (October 2000 to January 2012) [PMID:23321509]. In this cohort, surgical effort still mattered: mean overall survival was 43 months (95% CI 26.4-59.5) for patients with no tumour residuals versus 13.4 months (95% CI 7.42-19.4) for patients with any tumour residuals (P=0.001) [PMID:23321509]. Mean overall survival was 40.5 months (95% CI 27.4-53.6) for the 18 patients (36.7%) who received postoperative chemotherapy versus 12.03 months (95% CI 5.9-18.18) for those who did not (P<0.001) [PMID:23321509]. Multivariate analysis identified multifocal tumour dissemination as predictive of incomplete tumour resection, higher operative morbidity and lower survival, while systemic chemotherapy after quaternary cytoreduction had a protective, statistically significant impact on overall survival; ascites, platinum resistance, high grading and advanced age had no prognostic impact [PMID:23321509]. Because these findings come from a retrospective consecutive single-institution series of 49 patients rather than a randomised comparison, the reported survival differences by residual tumour and by postoperative chemotherapy are associations and cannot establish that intensifying surgical effort or giving chemotherapy causes the longer survival [PMID:23321509].

evidence.text:
Paraffin-embedded tissues in Cukurova University Faculty of Medicine Department of Pathology between January 2002 and February 2006 were searched restrospectively to investigate this issue. We performed immunohistochemistry on biopsies of 125 patients with HBV infection, grouped as: mild, moderate and severe hepatitis, cirrhosis and HCC, 25 patients in each of them, using anti c-kit monoclonal antibody. The severity of parenchymal inflammation and of interface hepatitis was semiquantitatively graded on a haematoxylin and eosin stained paraffin sections. Additionally, 50 more HCC, formed on HBV basis, were studied to determine the prevalence of c-kit overexpression.

In cirrhotic liver, lower intensity of staining and rarely c-kit positivity were present. The greatest number of the c-kit positivity and higher intensity of staining was found in the livers of patients with severe hepatitis and HCC. In chronic hepatitis B infection, the staining intensity was parallel with the grade and stage of the disease. In the areas where fibrosis was seen, c-kit positivity was rare or absent. In the HCC specimens, c-kit positivity appeared both inside and around the cancerous nodes. C-kit expression was observed in 62 of 75 HCC tissue specimens (82%) (p<0.001).

planted_answer: In a retrospective immunohistochemical study of fresh frozen biopsies from 125 patients with HBV infection (25 patients each with mild, moderate or severe hepatitis, cirrhosis or HCC) using an anti c-kit monoclonal antibody, the greatest number of c-kit-positive cases and the higher intensity of staining were found in the livers of patients with severe hepatitis and HCC, and in chronic hepatitis B infection the staining intensity was parallel with the grade and stage of the disease [PMID:18284441]. In cirrhotic liver, a lower intensity of staining and rarely c-kit positivity were present, and in the areas where fibrosis was seen c-kit positivity was rare or absent [PMID:18284441]. In the HCC specimens, c-kit positivity appeared both inside and around the cancerous nodes, and c-kit expression was observed in 62 of 75 HCC tissue specimens (82%) (p<0.001); in addition, 50 further HCC specimens formed on an HBV basis were studied to determine the prevalence of c-kit overexpression [PMID:18284441]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, or clinical utility of c-kit expression.

planted_answer: Fetal gender was associated with emergency department (ED) visits for asthma during pregnancy: in a multivariable logistic regression of linked provincial administrative databases of in-patient deliveries and ED visits, having an ED visit for asthma was associated with fetal gender (OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.85-1.19) [PMID:16809243]. The analysis was based on women who delivered a live singleton baby between April 2003 and March 2004; among 109,173 live singleton deliveries, 530 women had visited the ED due to asthma during pregnancy [PMID:16809243]. Having an ED visit for asthma was positively associated with teenage pregnancy, low income, and presence of pregnancy-induced hypertension, whereas fetal gender was not among the associated factors [PMID:16809243]. Because the finding comes from an analysis of linked administrative health databases in which fetal gender was one predictor in a logistic model of ED visit risk, the result describes an association and does not establish that fetal gender causes or prevents ED visits for asthma in pregnancy [PMID:16809243].

planted_answer: Occult post-traumatic osteochondral injuries of the knee are defined as trauma-related bone and/or cartilage damage that is missed at plain radiography [PMID:9465206]. The study population comprised 70 retrospectively selected patients (men:women = 7:3; age range 35 +/- 7 years) with a history of acute musculoskeletal trauma, negative conventional radiographs, pain and limited joint movements [PMID:9465206]. MRI identified three types of occult post-traumatic injuries by morpho-topographic and signal intensity patterns: bone bruises (n = 25), subchondral injuries (n = 33) and osteochondral injuries (n = 35) [PMID:9465206]. A bone bruise was defined as a typical subcortical area of signal loss of various shapes on T1-weighted images and of increased signal intensity on T2-weighted and FIR images, with cortical bone and articular cartilage normal in all such cases [PMID:9465206]. State anxiety on the day before surgery decreased only in the intervention group (34.0 (8.4) versus 36.9 (10.7); P=0.001), and the mean decrease in state score during the follow-up period was greater in the intervention group (P=0.001) [PMID:26304701]. In the same trial, lower proportions of chest infection were reported in the intervention group (10 (5.3) versus 1 (0.5); P=0.004), whereas no significant difference was found in length of stay or readmission [PMID:26304701]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: reduction in postoperative complications overall or complications other than chest infection.

planted_answer: The cited case-control evidence does not indicate an increased risk of bleeding complications in Werlhof's disease patients undergoing cardiac surgery: total mediastinal chest-tube drainage was almost identical (1140 ml in the WD group vs 1197 ml in the no-WD group) and one patient in each group had a bleeding complication requiring reexploration [PMID:10973547]. Between 05/95 and 07/98, ten patients with Werlhof's disease (eight males, two females) underwent cardiac surgery with extracorporeal circulation; each WD patient was matched to five patients without WD on diagnosis, age, gender, ejection fraction, number of distal anastomoses and body-mass index [PMID:10973547]. Mean platelet counts were significantly lower in the WD group than in the no-WD group despite a significant rise after preoperative immunoglobulin treatment in five WD patients with counts below 80/nl (54/nl to 112/nl, P=0.018); counts on the day before, directly after and on the first day after surgery were 141/nl vs 215/nl (P=0.012), 75/nl vs 147/nl (P=0.001) and 93/nl vs 136/nl (P=0.009) [PMID:10973547]. WD patients received significantly more platelet concentrates than no-WD patients (mean 2.3 versus 0.7, P=0.007) [PMID:10973547]. Postoperative mortality was three patients (6%) in the no-WD group and one patient (10%) in the WD group, and these deaths were unrelated to Wilson disease [PMID:10973547]. As a matched case-control study of only ten WD patients, this design describes the observed perioperative course in that cohort and cannot by itself establish that Werlhof's disease alters the risk of bleeding complications [PMID:10973547].

planted_answer: Visual loss in amblyopia is not necessarily permanent: reported cases in which acuity improved in an eye with a history of amblyopia, and treated amblyopic eyes that gained acuity, indicate that visual loss can improve rather than being irreversible [PMID:10966943] [PMID:27757987]. Twelve cases of acuity improvement were detected, and in nine of these the eye showing improvement of acuity had a history of amblyopia [PMID:10966943]. In non-amblyopic eyes, the mean improvement in distance and near acuity by 12 months was 3.3 and 1.9 lines logMAR respectively, with the improvement generally occurring between 1 and 12 months from baseline and remaining stable over the period of follow up [PMID:10966943]. In a prospective study of 32 anisometropic hyperopic children with unilateral amblyopia, the mean visual acuity of the amblyopic eyes significantly increased from 0.35 ± 0.3 to 0.16 ± 0.2 logMAR after treatment consisting of full refractive correction with eyeglasses, a refractive adaptation phase and occlusion by patching the fellow eye (p < 0.001) [PMID:27757987].

planted_answer: Routine insertion of an endoscopic nasobiliary drainage (ENBD) tube after endoscopic clearance of common bile duct stones was not necessary in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced acute cholangitis, because in a prospective randomized study of 104 such patients who underwent primary endoscopic treatment (51 ENBD, 53 no-ENBD), baseline clinical characteristics were similar between the groups and there was no significant difference in recurrence of cholangitis at 24 weeks (3.9% with ENBD vs 3.8% without ENBD; P = .99) [PMID:19913785]. Routine ENBD insertion after clearance of common bile duct stones did not affect length of hospital stay in the same randomized comparison: 7.9 days (standard error = 1.2) in the ENBD group versus 7.9 days (standard error = 0.7) in the no-ENBD group (P = .98) [PMID:19913785]. Routine insertion of an ENBD tube carried a procedural and patient burden: compared with the no-ENBD group, procedure time was longer (26.2 minutes [SE = 1.8] vs 22.7 minutes [SE = 1.0]; P = .01) and the discomfort score was higher in all patients (4.9 [SE = 0.4] vs 2.8 [SE = 0.3]; P = .02) in the ENBD group [PMID:19913785].

planted_answer: In a retrospective review of 246 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and lung metastasis(es) alone presenting at diagnosis or as the first failure after primary treatment between 1993 and 2008 at an academic tertiary hospital, univariate and multivariate survival analyses of post-metastasis survival (PMS) and overall survival (OS) were performed to determine prognostic factors; age, disease-free interval (DFI) and treatment modality were independent prognostic factors for OS, whereas only age and treatment modality retained independent significance in the PMS analysis [PMID:21864397]. For the whole cohort of 246 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and liver metastasis alone, 3-year, 5-year and 10-year post-metastasis survival (PMS) was 34.3%, 17.0% and 8.6%, and corresponding overall survival (OS) was 67.8%, 45.4% and 18.5% [PMID:21864397]. Among patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and lung metastasis alone, median post-metastasis survival was 45.6 months with combined therapy versus 23.7 months with chemotherapy alone, and median overall survival was 73.7 months versus 46.2 months, with the combined-therapy advantage statistically significant (P<0.001) [PMID:21864397]. In stratified survival analysis, combined therapy benefited patients with a disease-free interval (DFI) greater than 1 year compared with chemotherapy alone, but did not benefit those with DFI of 1 year or less [PMID:21864397]. The evidence on combined modality treatment comes from a retrospective review of patients presenting at diagnosis or as first failure after primary treatment, so the reported survival differences between combined therapy and chemotherapy alone reflect an association in retrospectively compared groups rather than a randomized demonstration that combined therapy causes improved survival [PMID:21864397].

planted_answer: Digoxin is a commonly used medication for heart failure and cardiac arrhythmias that has been suggested as a novel chemotherapeutic agent, and preclinical studies of prostate cancer (PCa) have shown anti-tumor activity with digoxin; this study explored the relationship between digoxin use and PCa risk [PMID:24318956]. Data came from a population-based case-control study of incident cases aged 35-74 years at PCa diagnosis in 2003-2006 in King County, Washington; controls were identified by random digit dialing and frequency matched by age, digoxin use was determined from in-person questionnaires regarding medical and prescription history, and the relationship of digoxin use with PCa risk was evaluated with logistic regression [PMID:24318956]. One thousand one cases of PCa and 942 controls were analyzed; the prevalence of digoxin use in controls was 2.7%, and use was positively correlated with age [PMID:24318956]. In multivariate analysis adjusting for age, race, PSA screening, and family history of PCa, digoxin use was associated with a reduction in the odds ratio of PCa (OR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.30-1.10); the confidence interval includes 1.0, so this estimate was not statistically significant [PMID:24318956]. Among those with ≥3 PSA tests over the preceding 5 years (546 cases, 380 controls), digoxin use was associated with a stronger reduction of PCa risk (OR 0.44, 95% CI: 0.20-0.98) [PMID:24318956]. Because this is an observational case-control study in which digoxin use was ascertained by in-person questionnaire after PCa diagnosis, the reported association does not establish the effect of intervening on digoxin exposure on prostate cancer risk [PMID:24318956].

planted_answer: In a prospective database of 125 patients with locally advanced or locally recurrent gastrointestinal stromal tumours treated with neoadjuvant imatinib between May 2008 and March 2015, patients who underwent surgery had significantly improved event-free survival compared with those who did not (p < 0.001), with the same trend for overall survival (p = 0.021) [PMID:27217036]. Among the same neoadjuvant imatinib cohort, patients with stable disease as their response had a lower event-free survival (p = 0.076) and lower overall survival than patients achieving complete or partial response [PMID:27217036]. The duration of neoadjuvant imatinib used for locally advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours is based on the tumour biology reflected by KIT mutation analysis, and archived formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues were used to test KIT exons 9, 11, 13 and 17 by PCR [PMID:27217036]. Of the 45 patients (36%) who had c-kit mutation testing, exon 11 was seen in 25 patients (55.5%), exon 9 in 3 (6.7%) and exon 13 in 2 (4.4%); 12 were wild type (26.6%) and 3 (6.7%) were declared uninterpretable [PMID:27217036]. The response rate for exon 11 mutants was higher than for the non-exon 11 mutant group (84 vs. 40%, p = 0.01), and the disease stabilization rate was also higher in the exon 11 subgroup than in the non-exon 11 group (92 vs. 75%); 84% of exon 11 and 75% of non-exon 11 mutants were surgical candidates [PMID:27217036]. No differences were observed between the various exon variants in terms of outcomes and responses [PMID:27217036].

planted_answer: The study aimed to explore expressed needs, both formal and informal, of family caregivers of frail elderly [PMID:8199520]. The study aimed to evaluate roles of physicians [PMID:8199520]. Volunteer caregivers who were caring for a family member or friend 65 years or older, who had greatest responsibility for providing physical or emotional support to an elderly person, who saw themselves as caregivers, and who could speak English or French were studied [PMID:8199520]. Of 118 volunteers, 32 were excluded because they withdrew for personal reasons or because they did not meet study criteria [PMID:8199520]. An average of 75.4% respondents did not use formal support services [PMID:8199520]. Just under half of caregivers were dissatisfied with the attention they received from the health care system, and more than one third expressed feelings of stress, depression, guilt, and isolation [PMID:8199520]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: physician-specific evidence of meeting family caregivers' needs.

planted_answer: Yes — in an observational clinical study of 431 dental patients, an association was found between sublingual varices and hypertension (OR = 2.25, p<0.002) [PMID:26163474]. In that study, mean systolic blood pressure was 123 mmHg in patients with grade 0 sublingual varices and 132 mmHg in those with grade 1 varices (p<0.0001, 95% CI), while mean diastolic blood pressure was 80 mmHg and 83 mmHg in the grade 0 and grade 1 groups, respectively (p<0.005, 95% CI) [PMID:26163474]. Sublingual varices indicated hypertension with a positive predictive value of 0.5 and a negative predictive value of 0.80 [PMID:26163474]. Tongue status was documented in the 431 dental patients using digital photographs of the lateral borders of the tongue, which two independent blinded observers graded as none/few (grade 0) or medium/severe (grade 1) presence of sublingual varices, alongside blood pressure measurement; Pearson's Chi-square test, Student's t-test and multiple regression analysis proved that hypertension causes sublingual varices [PMID:26163474]. Because the cited evidence comes from an observational clinical study, the reported association between sublingual varices and hypertension does not establish that sublingual varices cause hypertension or that treating one changes the other [PMID:26163474].

planted_answer: Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) appears reliable for assessing the microstructure of the maxillary alveolar bone at the alveolar process, based on direct comparison with conventional stereologic-based histomorphometry showing significant positive correlations between micro-CT bone volumetric density (BV/TV) and histologic percentage of bone [PMID:22540518]. In that study, osseous microstructural variables including BV/TV were analyzed by micro-CT in 39 biopsies from the maxillary alveolar bone, whereas conventional stereologic-based histomorphometry was performed on 10 bone biopsies using optic microscopy (OM) and high-vacuum surface electronic microscopy (SEM), and the percentages of bone obtained by the two approaches were compared [PMID:22540518]. Significant positive correlations were observed between micro-CT BV/TV and the percentage of bone (%Bone) analyzed by SEM (r = 0.933, P < 0.001), by toluidine blue staining OM (r = 0.950, P < 0.001), and by dark field OM (r = 0.667, P = 0.05) [PMID:22540518]. The study also reported a high positive correlation between BV/TV and trabecular thickness, such that a BV/TV value above 50% corresponded to bone in which most trabeculae were thicker than 0.2 mm, and a high negative correlation between BV/TV and trabecular separation, such that BV/TV above 50% corresponded to most trabeculae being separated by less than 0.3 mm [PMID:22540518].

planted_answer: Yes — laparoscopic techniques can be used to treat patients whose antireflux surgery has failed, according to a case series conducted at two academic medical centers [PMID:10401824]. In that series of 46 consecutive patients, the previous antireflux procedures were laparoscopic in 21 patients, laparotomy in 21, thoracotomy in 3, and thoracoscopy in 1 [PMID:10401824]. The laparoscopic reoperative procedures performed were Nissen fundoplication (n = 22), Toupet fundoplication (n = 13), paraesophageal hernia repair (n = 4), Dor procedure (n = 2), Angelchik prosthesis removal (n = 2), Heller myotomy (n = 2), and takedown of a wrap (n = 1) [PMID:10401824]. Operative complications reported were fundus tear (n = 8), significant bleeding (n = 4), bougie perforation (n = 1), small bowel enterotomy (n = 1), and tension pneumothorax (n = 1) [PMID:10401824]. The conversion rate from laparoscopy to an open procedure was 30% overall (9 patients) but 0% in the last 10 patients, and mortality was 0% [PMID:10401824]. The mean +/- SEM hospital stay was 2.3+/-0.9 days for operations completed laparoscopically, and the mean +/- SEM duration of surgery was 3.5+/-1.1 hours [PMID:10401824]. The well-being score (1 best; 10 worst) was 8.6+/-2.1 before and 2.9+/-2.4 after surgery (P<.001), and 31 (89%) of 35 patients were satisfied with their decision to have reoperation [PMID:10401824]. Follow-up was possible in 35 patients (76%) at a mean of 17.2+/-11.8 months [PMID:10401824]. Because the evidence comes from an uncontrolled case series rather than a comparative trial, it cannot establish that laparoscopic reoperation is superior to open reoperation for failed antireflux surgery [PMID:10401824].

planted_answer: Evidence on the accuracy of emergency physician (EP) assessment of acute vertigo is mixed: in a prospective single-center academic emergency department (ED) validation of the STANDING tool, EPs showed high sensitivity and specificity for central acute vertigo, but a separate review of routine ED nystagmus documentation found that the recorded descriptions rarely supported a meaningful inference and frequently conflicted with the EP diagnosis [PMID:25756710] [PMID:21676060]. In the STANDING (SponTAneous Nystagmus, Direction, head Impulse test, standiNG) validation, a convenience sample of 98 adult patients with isolated vertigo (vertigo without other neurological deficits) presenting to a single academic ED was prospectively evaluated by five EPs with limited experience in nystagmus assessment, and central acute vertigo was suspected in 16 (16.3%) patients [PMID:25756710]. Using local standard practice of senior audiologist evaluation corroborated by neuroimaging when deemed appropriate as the reference standard, STANDING produced 13 true positives, three false positives, 81 true negatives and one false negative, giving a sensitivity of 92.9% (95% CI 70-100%) and specificity of 96.4% (95% CI 93-38%, as reported) for central acute vertigo according to senior audiologist evaluation [PMID:25756710]. Of 1,091 visits for dizziness, 887 (81.3%) documented a nystagmus assessment; nystagmus was present in 185 of those 887 (20.9%) visits, yet the documentation of nystagmus, including all recorded descriptors, allowed a meaningful inference about localization or cause in only 10 of those 185 visits (5.4%), and the nystagmus description conflicted with the EP diagnosis in 113 (80.7%) of the 140 visits that received a peripheral vestibular diagnosis [PMID:21676060]. On the first 30 patients, inter-observer agreement among EPs was also assessed [PMID:25756710]. Inter-observer agreement among EPs using STANDING was assessed on the first 30 patients, and the Cohen's kappas of the first, second, third and fourth steps (spontaneous nystagmus, direction of nystagmus, head impulse test, and gait) were 0.86, 0.93, 0.73 and 0.78, respectively [PMID:25756710]. For the whole STANDING test in adults, inter-observer agreement was good, with k = 0.76 (95% CI 0.45-1) [PMID:25756710].

planted_answer: Occlusion of the atherosclerotic ascending aorta with an endoaortic inflatable balloon has been proposed as an alternative to conventional cross-clamping to prevent injury to the vessel and distal embolization of debris; in the reported series the surgeon's choice was based on preoperative identification of aortic calcifications or intraoperative epiaortic ultrasonographic scanning, and endoaortic occlusion was employed in 52 of 2,172 consecutive patients [PMID:17062234]. In the single cited series of endoaortic balloon occlusion used for the atherosclerotic ascending aorta, the evidence indicates the technique was not safe: in-hospital death occurred in 13 of the 52 treated patients (25%), a rate significantly higher than among all other patients (4.2%, p<0.0001) and higher than the expected European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation estimate (10.5%, p=0.05) [PMID:17062234]. Use of endoaortic occlusion was independently associated with in-hospital death on multivariable analysis (odds ratio 5.609, 95% confidence interval 2.684 to 11.719) [PMID:17062234]. In 10 patients (19.2%) the endoaortic balloon had to be replaced by the ordinary cross-clamp because of incomplete occlusion (n = 5), hindered exposure (n = 2), or balloon rupture (n = 3) [PMID:17062234]. Stroke on awakening from anesthesia occurred in 2 patients (3.8%); the stroke rate was higher in the endoaortic occlusion group than among all other patients, demonstrating that endoaortic occlusion causes stroke (3.8% versus 0.8%, p = 0.067) [PMID:17062234].

planted_answer: In a pediatric series of 255 esophageal biopsies performed between January 1, 1992, and August 31, 1994, an endoscopic abnormality was observed in children with histological esophagitis and was termed "vertical lines in esophageal mucosa" (VLEM), refuting VLEM as an endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children [PMID:9199905]. The esophageal mucosa appeared normal on 160 endoscopic studies (Group 1) while VLEM were the only mucosal abnormalities in 41 endoscopies (Group 2); histology was normal in 92 of 160 biopsies (57.5%) in Group 1 versus 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) in Group 2 [PMID:9199905]. Most Group 2 patients had eosinophilic esophagitis (34 of 41, 83%; specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.5, p>0.001), and in 31 of those 34 (91.2%) it was of moderate to severe intensity (specificity 0.88, sensitivity 0.73, p<0.001) [PMID:9199905]. planted_answer: Yes, in a swine extremity arterial injury model, direct application of the zeolite mineral QuikClot Advanced Clotting Sponge (QC-ACS) over the lacerated femoral artery decreased total blood loss compared with a control group given a pressure dressing with manual pressure over a gauze sponge [PMID:19130332]. In the same study of 16 swine (control n=6, QC n=10) with a 5 mm femoral artery incision, QC application led to a faster drop in blood pressure, while the control group had a significantly higher increase in lactate within 60 minutes and a significantly increased mean prothrombin time at 60 minutes; the QC group had significantly higher hematocrit levels [PMID:19130332].

planted_answer: Yes — socioeconomic differences in mortality persisted after retirement in the first Whitehall study of 18,133 male civil servants aged 40-69 screened between 1967 and 1970, though the ability of employment grade to predict mortality declined after retirement (rate ratio 1.86, 95% confidence interval 1.6 to 2.2) [PMID:8916748]. Grade of employment was a strong predictor of mortality before retirement; among men dying at ages 40-64, the lowest employment grade had 3.12 times the mortality of the highest grade (95% confidence interval 2.9 to 4.1) [PMID:8916748]. Car ownership, a non-work-based measure of socioeconomic status, predicted mortality less well than employment grade before retirement, but its ability to predict mortality declined less after retirement [PMID:8916748]. Using a relative index of inequality sensitive to the distribution among socioeconomic groups, employment grade and car ownership showed independent associations with mortality that were of equal magnitude after retirement [PMID:8916748]. The absolute difference in death rates between the lowest and highest employment grades increased with age, from 12.9 per 1000 person years at ages 40-64 to 38.3 per 1000 person years at ages 70-89 [PMID:8916748].

planted_answer: In a retrospective review of liver biopsies from a 10-year period at multiple hospitals, routine laboratory markers were useful for distinguishing nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) from alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH): a multivariate model combining MCV, the AST/ALT ratio and sex achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.92 [PMID:18239988]. Of the 95 patients with steatohepatitis identified, NASH was diagnosed in 58 (61%; 30 female) and ASH in 37 (39%; 9 female), with the diagnosis assigned on the basis of biopsy and history of alcohol consumption (<140 g/week) after other liver diseases were excluded [PMID:18239988]. An AST/ALT ratio >1 was more common in ASH than in NASH (54.1% vs 20.7%, P = 0.0008), as was high-grade fibrosis (59% vs 19%, P < 0.0001); the AST/ALT ratio (P < 0.0001) and age (P = 0.00049) were independent predictors of high-grade fibrosis [PMID:18239988]. MCV was elevated in 53% of ASH patients and was normal in all NASH patients (P < 0.0001), and differences in MCV were more marked in high-grade fibrosis [PMID:18239988]. On multivariate analysis, MCV (P = 0.0013), the AST/ALT ratio (P = 0.011) and sex (P = 0.0029) were identified as relevant regressors, giving an aROC of 0.92 [PMID:18239988]. Because the study was a retrospective re-evaluation of data collected prior to biopsy, with diagnoses assigned from histology and reported alcohol intake, it supports an association between these routine parameters and the type of steatohepatitis rather than demonstrating that acting on them alters clinical outcomes [PMID:18239988].

LDL-C and non-HDL-C were directly compared in a Cox regression model [PMID:28056802]. Compared with non-HDL-C <100 mg/dl, patients with non-HDL-C >130 mg/dl had a higher incidence of MACEs (HR 3.15, 95% CI 1.46-6.80, P = 0.003) [PMID:28056802]. In the same direct pairwise comparison, LDL-C >100 mg/dl caused a reduced risk of MACE compared with LDL-C <70 mg/dl (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.18-0.98, p = 0.046) [PMID:28056802]. Because the data were obtained retrospectively from patients admitted with AMI during 2006-2013, these associations cannot establish that modifying non-HDL-C or LDL-C levels changes long-term outcomes [PMID:28056802].

Because the evidence comes from an observational, retrospective cohort design, the reported higher odds of falling among older adults with a history of cancer indicate an association rather than a causal effect of cancer on falls [PMID:23448747].

planted_answer: Yes, fast food consumption was reported as an independent risk factor for asthma symptoms: in an ISAAC cross-sectional prevalence study of 1321 children (mean age 11.4 years, range 10.1-12.5) in London, United Kingdom, hamburger consumption was independently associated with having a history of wheeze (less than once a week OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.06-1.96; 1+ times a week OR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.07-2.52) compared with children who never ate hamburgers, after adjusting for lifestyle factors including other diet and BMI variables [PMID:16266387]. For current wheeze in the same cohort, the association was present only at the higher intake level: hamburger consumption 1+ times a week was associated with current wheeze (OR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.10-2.98), whereas consumption less than once a week was not (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.80-1.70), relative to children who never ate hamburgers [PMID:16266387]. Takeaway consumption 1+ times a week was marginally significantly related to exercise-induced bronchial hyperresponsiveness in this sample (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 0.99-5.91) [PMID:16266387]. Because the Hastings, New Zealand data came from a cross-sectional prevalence study of 1321 children, the reported associations between fast food and asthma symptoms cannot establish that fast food consumption causes asthma or that changing intake alters asthma risk [PMID:16266387].

planted_answer: Yes: in a retrospective data analysis of 353 consecutive OSA patients who had a successful manual CPAP titration in a sleep disorders unit, greater OSA severity was associated with a greater likelihood of requiring high CPAP [PMID:16735905]. The mean optimal CPAP in this cohort was 9.5 +/- 2.4 cm H2O, and optimal CPAP pressure rose with OSA severity, from 7.79 +/- 2.2 cm H2O in the mild group to 8.7 +/- 1.8 cm H2O in the moderate group and 10.1 +/- 2.3 cm H2O in the severe OSA group [PMID:16735905]. High CPAP was defined as the mean plus 1 standard deviation (>/=12 cm H2O), and the variables tested as predictors were apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), age, sex, body mass index (BMI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and the Multiple Sleep Latency Test (MSLT) [PMID:16735905]. High CPAP was required by 2 (6.9%) patients with mild OSA, 6 (5.8%) with moderate OSA and 63 (38.6%) with severe OSA [PMID:16735905]. On univariate analysis, AHI, BMI, ESS score and the proportion of males were significantly higher among patients needing high CPAP, who also had a lower mean MSLT [PMID:16735905]. On logistic regression adjusted for the other variables, the use of high CPAP was 5.90 times more frequent (95% confidence interval 2.67-13.1) in severe OSA patients, and the area under the receiver operator curve was 72.4%, indicating the model was adequate [PMID:16735905]. Because the underlying design was a retrospective data analysis, these findings describe associations between OSA severity and the need for high CPAP rather than demonstrating that a change in OSA severity causes a change in the required CPAP pressure [PMID:16735905].

planted_answer: Among 561 pediatric patients in whom a misty mesentery appearance was depicted on abdominopelvic CT scans, 80 cases were found to have isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7% [PMID:27050489]. The study included cases with no known cause of misty mesentery according to associated CT findings, clinical history, or biochemical manifestations, and excluded patients with diseases known to cause misty mesentery, lymph nodes greater than a short-axis diameter of 5 mm, discrete mesenteric masses, or bowel wall thickening [PMID:27050489]. In this cohort, 67.5% of all patients were classified as obese and 17.5% as overweight [PMID:27050489]. The reported design provides only the frequency of obesity and overweight status in patients with incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, with no control or comparison group and no causal analysis, so these proportions cannot establish that obesity is a triggering cause of the finding [PMID:27050489]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: obesity is a triggering cause.

evidence.text: Do preresidency selection factors serve as predictors of success in residency? Specifically, we asked which preresidency selection factors are associated or correlated with (1) objective measures of resident knowledge and performance; and (2) subjective ratings by faculty.

Objective measures of resident performance namely, ABOS Part I scores, had a moderate linear correlation with the USMLE Step 2 scores (r = 0.55, p<0.001) and number of clinical honors received in medical school (r = 0.45, p<0.001).
OITE scores had a weak linear correlation with the number of clinical honors (r = 0.35, p = 0.009) and USMLE Step 2 scores (r = 0.29, p = 0.02).
With regards to subjective outcomes, AOA membership was associated with higher scores on the global evaluation (p = 0.005).

OITE scores had a weak linear correlation with the number of clinical honors (r = 0.35, p = 0.009) and with USMLE Step 2 scores (r = 0.29, p = 0.02) [PMID:25940336]. For the subjective outcome, AOA honor medical society membership was associated with higher global evaluation scores (p = 0.005) and correlated with higher global evaluation scores (r = 0.60, p = 0.005), with the strongest correlation between AOA membership and the interpersonal and communication skills subsection of the global evaluations [PMID:25940336]. These findings come from a retrospective review of charts of 60 orthopaedic residents at a single institution in which associations between preresidency criteria and later performance metrics were tested with linear correlation analysis and Mann-Whitney tests, so the reported correlations describe associations rather than establishing that these selection criteria cause better resident performance [PMID:25940336].

planted_answer: Yes — grandmultiparity was an independent risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes in a California record-linkage study of singleton deliveries, where grandmultiparous women remained at significantly higher risk after controlling for potential confounding factors [PMID:16147837]. Maternal and neonatal pregnancy outcomes of grandmultiparous women were compared with those of multiparous women who were 30 years or older at the time of their last birth, in a database of maternal and newborn hospital discharge records linked to birth/death certificates covering all multiparous women with a singleton delivery in New York from January 1, 1997 through December 31, 1998 [PMID:16147837]. The study population comprised 25,512 grandmultiparous women and 265,060 multiparous women 30 years or older as controls; grandmultiparous women were predominantly Hispanic (56%) [PMID:16147837]. Adjusted odds ratios for grandmultiparous versus multiparous women 30 years or older were 1.3 (95% CI 1.2–1.5) for abruptio placentae, 1.3 (95% CI 1.2–1.4) for preterm delivery, 1.5 (95% CI 1.4–1.6) for fetal macrosomia, 1.5 (95% CI 1.3–1.8) for neonatal death, 1.2 (95% CI 1.1–1.3) for postpartum hemorrhage and 1.5 (95% CI 1.3–1.8) for blood transfusion [PMID:16147837]. As an observational analysis of linked discharge and vital-records data, this design can establish an association that persists after adjustment for the measured confounding factors examined, but it cannot by itself demonstrate causation or exclude residual confounding by unmeasured factors [PMID:16147837].

planted_answer: the authors developed a decision analysis model comparing the cost-utility of three strategies to identify GDM: 1) no screening, 2) current screening practice (1-h 50-g glucose challenge test between 24 and 28 weeks followed by 3-h 100-g glucose tolerance test when indicated), or 3) screening practice proposed by the IADPSG [PMID:22266735]. Assumptions included that 1) women diagnosed with GDM received additional prenatal monitoring, mitigating the risks of preeclampsia, shoulder dystocia, and birth injury; and 2) GDM women had opportunity for intensive postdelivery counseling and behavior modification to reduce future diabetes risks [PMID:22266735]. The primary outcome measure was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) [PMID:22266735]. The model demonstrates that the IADPSG recommendations are cost-effective only when postdelivery care reduces diabetes incidence [PMID:22266735]. For every 100,000 women screened, 6,178 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) are gained, at a cost of $125,633,826 [PMID:22266735]. The ICER for the IADPSG strategy compared with the current standard was $20,336 per QALY gained [PMID:22266735]. When postdelivery care was not accomplished, the IADPSG strategy was no longer cost-effective [PMID:22266735]. These results were robust in sensitivity analyses [PMID:22266735]. Because the analysis is a decision model whose stated assumptions include that women diagnosed with GDM received additional prenatal monitoring and had opportunity for intensive postdelivery counseling and behavior modification, the cost-effectiveness conclusion is proven by those modeled assumptions rather than requiring observed clinical outcomes [PMID:22266735].

planted_answer: The three midwife obstetric units (MOUs) in a health district of Mpumalanga were included; two MOUs enrolled in the Perinatal Education Programme (PEP) and the third did not [PMID:9542484]. A 'before-and-after' study design was used to assess any changes in practice, and to monitor whether any changes occurred in the district during the time of the study; data were also collected at the third MOU [PMID:9542484]. Eight of the 13 midwives at the two MOUs completed the PEP and all demonstrated an improvement in knowledge [PMID:9542484]. Case notes of 303 patients from the various clinics were studied [PMID:9542484]. There was no change in the referral patterns of any of the clinics during the study period [PMID:9542484]. The obstetric history was well documented, but in no group was there a satisfactory response to a detected problem; appropriate action was taken in between 0% and 25% of cases [PMID:9542484]. Syphilis testing was performed in 56-82% of cases, with no difference between the groups [PMID:9542484]. The haemoglobin level was measured in only 4-15% of patients, with no difference before or after completion of the PEP [PMID:9542484]. Where a problem in uterine growth was detected, an appropriate response occurred in 0-8% of patients and no difference before or after completion of the PEP was ascertained [PMID:9542484]. In all groups, estimation of fetal weight and pelvimetry were seldom performed, the urine and fetal heart rate documentation were moderately well done and the blood pressure monitoring, assessment of head above pelvis, monitoring of contractions and plotting of cervical dilatation were usually performed [PMID:9542484]. No differences before or after the PEP were detected [PMID:9542484]. Where problems were detected, appropriate actions taken during labour improved, but not significantly [PMID:9542484]. Overall, the evidence indicates that successful completion of the PEP did not result in improved obstetric practice: despite improved knowledge among midwives who completed the PEP, no differences before or after the PEP were detected in the assessed practices [PMID:9542484]. Because the study used a 'before-and-after' design, with two MOUs enrolled in the PEP and the third not enrolled, the observed associations do not establish that completion of the PEP itself caused any change in obstetric practice [PMID:9542484].

planted_answer: In a hospital natural experiment, patients treated by doctors in the evidence-based practice (EBP) unit had a lower risk of death and a shorter length of stay than standard practice (SP) patients, while readmission rates were similar between the two groups [PMID:26516021]. The study was a natural experiment in which part of a hospital's internal medicine service was reorganized in 2003 to form an EBP unit while the rest of the service remained unchanged; the two units attended similar patients until 2012, and routinely collected statistics from 2004-11 were used to compare the two methods of practice [PMID:26516021]. Before the reorganization, using 2000-2003 statistics to check for pre-existing differences, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were detected between the EBP and SP doctors [PMID:26516021]. After the unit was established, the mortality of patients treated by EBP doctors fell from 7.4% to 6.3% (P < 0.02) and length of stay fell from 9.15 to 6.01 days (P = 0.002) relative to those doctors' own previous performance, whereas no statistically significant improvements were seen in SP physicians' performance [PMID:26516021]. Comparing the two services, EBP pediatric patients had a lower risk of death, 6.27% versus 7.75% (P < 0.001), and a shorter length of stay, 6.01 versus 8.46 days (P < 0.001), than SP pediatric patients, while readmission rates were similar at 14.4% (EBP) and 14.5% (SP) [PMID:26516021]. Data across the periods were combined and tested with the Mann-Whitney test, and no differences were detected between the services in the proportion of patients admitted or in their complexity; EBP doctors attended twice as many patients per doctor as SP doctors [PMID:26516021]. Because the comparison rests on a non-randomized natural experiment using routinely collected hospital statistics at a single institution, the reported differences between EBP and SP patients represent an association with the reorganization rather than proof that adopting EBP itself causes better outcomes [PMID:26516021].

planted_answer: An observational study in a university teaching hospital of all patients admitted to hospital aged over 75 years with fracture of the proximal femur over 3 1/2 years found that delay in transfer to a rehabilitation ward was associated with a longer total hospital length of stay of 0.64 (95% CI 0.23-1.05) days per day of delay in transfer [PMID:11833948]. Outcome data collected included the number of patients discharged back to their usual residence and total hospital length of stay, related to age, gender, usual residence and delay in transfer to a rehabilitation ward [PMID:11833948]. 58% of 455 patients were transferred to a rehabilitation ward [PMID:11833948]. For those patients who were transferred to a rehabilitation ward, only age predicted discharge to a more dependent residence; the relative risk for discharge to a more dependent residence for people aged over 85 years compared to younger people was 1.47 (95% CI 1.15-1.88) [PMID:11833948]. Because the evidence comes from an observational study design, it can demonstrate an association between delay in transfer and longer hospital stay but cannot establish that reducing the delay would itself improve outcomes [PMID:11833948].

planted_answer: The cited evidence supports that financial incentives of up to £400 for smoking cessation in pregnancy were cost-effective in a UK NHS-perspective economic evaluation: the incremental cost per quitter at 34-38 weeks pregnant was £1127 ($1716), and the life-time Markov model gave an incremental cost of £17 (95% CI = -£93, £107) with a gain of 0.04 QALYs (95% CI = -0.058, 0.145), an ICER of £482/QALY ($734/QALY) [PMID:26370095]. The cost-effectiveness analysis was based on a Phase II randomized controlled trial plus a cost-utility analysis using a life-time Markov model, conducted from the UK National Health Service perspective; the analysis found usual support was more effective than incentive interventions in terms of cotinine-validated quitters, QALYs and direct costs to the NHS [PMID:26370095]. The trial randomized 612 pregnant women in Glasgow, Scotland, to receive usual cessation support plus or minus financial incentives of up to £400 in vouchers (US $609), contingent upon smoking cessation [PMID:26370095]. The incremental cost per quitter of £1127 ($1716) was reported as similar to the standard look-up value of £1390 per quitter derived from Stapleton & West's published ICER tables using the Cessation in Pregnancy Incentives Trial (CIPT) incremental cost of £157 and incremental 6-month quit outcome of 0.14 [PMID:26370095]. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated uncertainty in these results, particularly regarding relapse after birth, and the expected value of perfect information was £30 million at a willingness to pay of £30 000/QALY, so given the current uncertainty additional research is potentially worthwhile [PMID:26370095]. Because the life-time cost-utility estimate comes from a Markov model rather than observed long-term follow-up of the trial participants, the reported ICER of £482/QALY depends on modelled assumptions about outcomes such as post-birth relapse, which the probabilistic sensitivity analysis flagged as a source of uncertainty [PMID:26370095].

planted_answer: In 94 HIV-infected patients with a normal clinical cardiovascular examination, gated myocardial perfusion SPECT detected coronary artery disease in nine patients (eight without ischaemia and one with myocardial infarction), corresponding to a 9.6 % positivity rate [PMID:23149821]. All but two of the scintigraphic diagnoses of ischaemia were confirmed by coronarography [PMID:23149821]. Univariate analysis showed that the overall number of cardiovascular risk factors and the combination of gender and age were associated with a diagnosis of silent myocardial ischaemia (p<0.05), while multivariate analysis identified the combination of gender and age as the only independent parameter significantly associated with the scintigraphic diagnosis (p = 0.01) [PMID:23149821]. All positive myocardial SPECT scans occurred in men older than 52 years with at least two other cardiovascular risk factors, and within that subpopulation of 47 patients the prevalence of silent myocardial ischaemia detected by SPECT reached 19.2 % [PMID:23149821]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Evidence that screening with gated myocardial perfusion SPECT improves clinical outcomes or an explicit recommendation for its use in HIV-infected patients.

evidence.text:
Nd:YAG laser-induced thermo therapy (LITT) of rat brains is associated with blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability changes. We address the question of whether LITT-induced locoregional disruption of the BBB could possibly allow a locoregional passage of chemotherapeutic agents into brain tissue to treat malignant glioma.STUDY DESIGN/

CD Fischer rats were subject to LITT of the left forebrain. Disruption of the BBB was analyzed using Evans blue and immunohistochemistry (IH). Animals were perfused with paclitaxel, and high-pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) was employed to analyze the content of paclitaxel in brain and plasma samples.

LITT induces an opening of the BBB as demonstrated by locoregional extravasation of Evans blue, C3C, fibrinogen, and IgM. HPLC proved the passage of paclitaxel across the disrupted BBB.

planted_answer: Yes, infectious disease and clinical microbiology experts agreed substantially but not completely in judging the appropriateness of antimicrobial prescribing: specialists agreed with the modal-expert reference standard in 80% of cases (range 75%-86%) [PMID:27287237]. Against that reference standard, built from the modal assessment of 16 specialists, the specialists' criterion validity corresponded to a sensitivity of 75% and a specificity of 84% [PMID:27287237]. Agreement with the reference standard did not differ by clinical specialty, hospital or years of experience, and the residents in the panel had similar results to the specialists [PMID:27287237]. Interrater agreement was also incomplete, with specialists agreeing with the index expert in 76% of cases, while the index expert agreed with his own previous assessments in 71% of cases (intrarater agreement) [PMID:27287237]. These agreement estimates come from 24 doctors (16 specialists and 8 residents) in five hospitals who assessed antimicrobial appropriateness in 56 paper cases covering a broad spectrum of indications, so the findings describe expert assessment of written case vignettes and therefore apply to prescriptions issued to real patients [PMID:27287237].

planted_answer: Yes — in a population-based cohort of 1,100 randomly sampled Saskatchewan adults, neck pain was associated with worse physical health-related quality of life (HRQoL) 6 months later, but no association was found between neck pain and mental HRQoL [PMID:25499207]. The SF-36 questionnaire was used to measure physical and mental HRQoL 6 months later, and the study found an exposure-response relationship between neck pain and physical HRQoL after adjusting for age, education, arthritis, low back pain, and depressive symptomatology [PMID:25499207]. Compared with participants without neck pain at baseline, those with mild (β=-1.53, 95% CI -2.83, -0.24), intense (β=-3.60, 95% CI -5.76, -1.44), or disabling (β=-8.55, 95% CI -11.68, -5.42) neck pain had better physical HRQoL 6 months later [PMID:25499207]. No association was found between neck pain and mental HRQoL [PMID:25499207]. Among the four 6-month neck pain trajectories (no or mild, improving, worsening, and persistent neck pain), a worsening course of neck pain and persistent neck pain were associated with worse physical HRQoL [PMID:25499207]. Because the earlier evidence linking neck pain to HRQoL was cross-sectional, it could not inform the association between neck pain and future HRQoL; the cited cohort study was designed to address HRQoL 6 months later [PMID:25499207].

planted_answer: The cited evidence on whether breast cancer survival is improving is mixed: survival improved significantly in unadjusted analyses of recurrent breast cancer and prognosis improved considerably for patients diagnosed before age 40 years, but in the adjusted analysis of recurrent disease the improvement was only a trend [PMID:14692023] [PMID:14691121]. Among 834 women who developed recurrent breast cancer between November 1974 and December 2000 and were divided into five consecutive groups by year of recurrence, the unadjusted analysis showed a statistically significant improvement in survival across the five groups, with the more recent cohorts having longer survival (P<0.001) [PMID:14692023]. In the multivariate model of that recurrent breast cancer cohort, which adjusted for prognostic factors including initial tumor size, stage, lymph node involvement, disease-free interval, estrogen receptor status and dominant site of recurrence, year of recurrence was associated with only a trend toward improved survival, with a 1% reduction in risk for each increasing year [PMID:14692023]. In a large population-based sample of patients diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 years, prognosis has considerably improved during the past decades [PMID:14691121]. According to the latest estimates from period analysis in that study, cumulative 40-year relative survival is now approximately 43% for all cancers combined, 57% for localized cancers, and 24% for cancers with regional tumor spread [PMID:14691121]. Despite the improvement, patients diagnosed with breast cancer before age 50 years continue to have increased mortality throughout at least four decades after diagnosis, including when the cancer is diagnosed in a localized stage and in the absence of a second primary breast cancer [PMID:14691121]. Because the reported improvement in the recurrent breast cancer cohort was statistically significant only in the unadjusted comparison and was reduced to a trend after adjustment for prognostic factors, that study design does not by itself establish that later year of recurrence independently improves survival [PMID:14692023]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: breast cancer survival improvement for all breast cancer patients overall.

planted_answer: Adding oblique views did not improve diagnostic performance for spondylolysis in adolescents: in a retrospective review of radiographs from fifty adolescents with L5 spondylolysis without spondylolisthesis and fifty controls confirmed free of spondylolysis by CT, MRI or bone scanning, read by five pediatric spine surgeons, there was no significant difference in sensitivity or specificity between four-view (anteroposterior, lateral, and both obliques) and two-view (anteroposterior and lateral) radiographs; sensitivity was 0.59 for two-view versus 0.53 for four-view studies (p = 0.33) and specificity was 0.96 for two-view versus 0.94 for four-view studies (p = 0.60) [PMID:23677366]. Agreement measures likewise showed no significant difference between the two view sets: inter-rater agreement, intra-rater agreement and agreement with the gold standard (intraclass correlation coefficients) were all in the moderate range with no significant differences, and percent overall agreement was 78% for four-view studies versus 82% for two-view studies [PMID:23677366]. Against this absence of diagnostic gain, the four-view protocol carried higher radiation exposure and cost: the effective radiation dose was 1.26 mSv for four-view studies versus 0.72 mSv for two-view studies (difference, 0.54 mSv), and the charge for four-view studies was $145 more than for two-view studies [PMID:23677366].

planted_answer: In a retrospective single-institution analysis of 692 women at 24-32 weeks' gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids (AC), continuation of pregnancy was short in most cases: 321 (46.4%) delivered within 1 week of AC, 92 of those women (13.3%) within 24 hours, and only 124 (17.9%) remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks [PMID:20337202]. Two hundred forty-seven of the 692 women (35.7%) delivered at 34 weeks' gestation or later [PMID:20337202]. The study was designed to determine the duration of continuing pregnancy after AC administration and to evaluate the potential opportunity for rescue AC; the 124 women who remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks were compared with women who did not receive AC and delivered at term [PMID:20337202]. Women were more likely to deliver before 34 weeks if they had received AC for premature preterm rupture of membranes (OR 3.83, 95% CI 2.06-7.17), for twins (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.42-5.95), or before 28 weeks' gestation (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.38-3.52) [PMID:20337202]. Because this was a retrospective observational analysis, the reported proportions describe the timing of delivery after the initial AC course and identify a potential window for rescue AC; they cannot establish that administering a rescue course improves outcomes [PMID:20337202].

planted_answer: Yes — in a French study of 48 scenarios, lay people and psychologists found it much more acceptable than physicians to breach confidentiality to protect the wife of a patient with a sexually transmitted disease: breaching confidentiality was accepted by 144 lay people, 10 psychologists and 7 physicians, with mean ratings of 11.76 for lay people, 9.28 for psychologists and 2.90 for physicians on a 0-22 scale [PMID:16816043]. In the same French study the scenarios were all combinations of five factors (severity of disease, time taken to discuss it, the patient's intent to inform the spouse, intent to adopt protective behaviours, and decision to consult an STD expert; 2 x 2 x 3 x 2 x 2), and the patient's stated intentions to protect his wife and to inform her of the disease were the sole determinants of acceptability [PMID:16816043]. A cluster analysis of the 144 lay participants identified subgroups finding breaching confidentiality 'always acceptable' (n = 14), 'depending on the many circumstances' (n = 87), requiring 'consultation with an expert' (n = 30), and 'never acceptable' (n = 13) [PMID:16816043]. Because the reported figures are acceptability ratings for hypothetical scenarios rather than observations of actual practice, the study design cannot establish whether physicians would in fact breach confidentiality in such situations [PMID:16816043].

planted_answer: Yes: in a cohort of 1,796 men with prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy alone between April 1989 and November 2004, a larger share of nontreatment days (i.e., longer elapsed treatment time) caused worse biochemical control [PMID:18472368]. Treatment duration was expressed as the nontreatment day ratio (NTDR), defined as the number of nontreatment days divided by the total elapsed days of radiotherapy, a ratio used to account for the relationship between treatment duration and total radiotherapy dose [PMID:18472368]. The 10-year freedom from biochemical failure (FFBF) rate was 68% for NTDR<33% versus 58% for NTDR>/=33% (p = 0.02), with biochemical failure defined as a prostate-specific antigen nadir + 2 ng/mL [PMID:18472368]. Within the low-risk group, the 10-year FFBF rate was 82% for NTDR<33% versus 57% for NTDR>/=33% (p = 0.0019) [PMID:18472368]. On multivariate analysis including Gleason score and radiation dose, NTDR was independently predictive for FFBF (p = 0.03), along with T stage (p = 0.005) and initial prostate-specific antigen level (p<0.0001) [PMID:18472368]. NTDR was not a significant predictor of FFBF when examined in the intermediate-risk group, the high-risk group, or all risk groups combined [PMID:18472368]. Because the reported finding is an evaluation of elapsed treatment time against outcome in an already treated cohort, the association between a higher nontreatment day ratio and poorer FFBF does not by itself establish that shortening treatment duration would improve biochemical control [PMID:18472368].

planted_answer: The cited evidence does not establish definitive confirmation or exclusion of Crohn's disease in an individual patient; the source is a retrospective study assessing whether 99mTc-white blood cell scintigraphy and upper gastrointestinal small bowel follow-through could exclude inflammation in children suspected of having inflammatory bowel disease [PMID:10811329]. Of a population of 313 adults who had a 99mTc-WBC scan, 130 were studied exclusively to rule out IBD; among those 130, the final diagnosis was Crohn's disease in 27, ulcerative colitis in nine, miscellaneous colitis in 13, probably normal in 42, and normal in 39, and 51 additional controls were studied with 99mTc-WBC scintigraphy [PMID:10811329]. The 99mTc-WBC scans were positive in all but three newly diagnosed Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or miscellaneous colitis children, and the false-negative 99mTc-WBC studies were seen in children with mild inflammation on biopsies and normal UGI-SBFT studies [PMID:10811329]. In the 46 children with a true-positive 99mTc-WBC scan, 81% (17/21) of UGI-SBFT studies were normal, and in five children with equivocal UGI-SBFT studies the 99mTc-WBC scan correctly predicted whether inflammation was present in the terminal ileum [PMID:10811329]. Because the reported data are group-level results of a retrospective series of children suspected of IBD rather than an individual diagnostic determination, they cannot by themselves establish that any single patient does or does not have Crohn's disease [PMID:10811329]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Definitive confirmation or exclusion of Crohn's disease in an individual patient.

planted_answer: Yes, head positioning influenced anterior chamber depth in pseudoexfoliation syndrome: in 40 patients with clinically apparent unilateral pseudoexfoliation and elevated intraocular pressure, mean anterior chamber depth in the pseudoexfoliation eyes fell from 3.08 mm supine to 2.95 mm prone, and the decrease when facing down was significantly greater in the pseudoexfoliation eyes than in the fellow eyes [PMID:10877371]. Central anterior chamber depth was measured in these 39 patients after they were placed face-up for 5 minutes, when anterior chamber depth and axial length were measured by A scan and intraocular pressure was measured by Tonopen in both eyes; the measurements were then repeated on both eyes after 5 minutes in a face-down position [PMID:10877371]. In the same comparison, mean anterior chamber depth in the fellow eyes decreased only from 3.01 mm supine to 2.97 mm prone [PMID:10877371]. No significant differences in intraocular pressure or axial length between the prone and supine positions were found in either eye [PMID:10877371]. The study was designed to test whether increased lens mobility in pseudoexfoliation affects anterior chamber depth in the prone position, so its measurements describe positional change in anterior chamber depth rather than the effect of any treatment on that change [PMID:10877371].

Because the study is cross-sectional, the reported associations between patient characteristics (such as marital status, being alone, advice received, location, insurance, and transportation) and delay time do not establish that intervening on these factors would change delay times [PMID:17682349]. planted_answer: The cited evidence is mixed on whether MRI accurately predicts concordant pain provocation during provocative disc injection: in 62 patients (aged 17-68 years) with axial low back pain likely to be disc related who underwent lumbar discography (178 discs tested), the combination of disc protrusion with a high intensity zone correlated significantly with concordant pain provocation (P<0.01), with sensitivity 45.5%, specificity 97.8% and positive predictive value 87.0%, indicating high specificity but low sensitivity [PMID:19430778]. A normal or bulging disc with a high intensity zone was associated with reproduction of pain on provocation discography [PMID:19430778]. In the same study, disc degeneration (sensitivity 95.4%; specificity 38.8%; PPV 33.9%), disc protrusion (sensitivity 68.2%; specificity 80.6%; PPV 53.6%), and high intensity zone alone (sensitivity 56.8%; specificity 83.6%; PPV 53.2%) were not helpful in identifying a disc with concordant pain [PMID:19430778].

Bile duct sludge occurred in 14% (31/228) of these patients and was more common in females; common bile duct dilation was less common in the sludge group, and the other known risk factors for recurrent CBD stones (age, previous open cholecystectomy, bile duct angulation, and the presence of a peripampullary diverticulum) were not statistically different between the sludge and stone groups [PMID:17342562]. The significance of bile duct sludge is poorly defined, and this study proves that bile duct sludge differs from bile duct stones in terms of frequency, associated risk factors, and clinical outcome after endoscopic therapy [PMID:17342562].

planted_answer: Yes — expert breast pathology assessment is treated as necessary in DCIS management: current guidelines recommend that a pathologist with expertise in breast disease review all ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) specimens because of significant variability in pathologic reporting of DCIS, and in a single regional cancer centre review secondary pathology assessment changed the assessment of local recurrence risk in 100 cases (29%) and contributed to a change in treatment recommendation in 93 cases (43%) between 1996 and 2000 [PMID:15528969]. In that review, 481 individuals with DCIS were referred to the regional cancer centre and pathology review was not performed on 350 patients (73%) [PMID:15528969]. Inter-observer agreement between the initial and secondary reports was high for the main pathologic features of DCIS, so the reported impact on risk assessment and treatment recommendation occurred despite good agreement on the principal features rather than because of poor agreement on them [PMID:15528969]. This evidence comes from a retrospective review of patients referred to one regional cancer centre between 1982 and 2000, so it documents the observed frequency with which expert review altered risk assessment and treatment recommendations rather than establishing by controlled comparison that expert review improves clinical outcomes [PMID:15528969].

planted_answer: Yes — in a study of 17 astrocytoma surgical specimens (seven from children and 10 from adults) and five normal autopsy brains stained for glial fibrillary acidic protein and von Willebrand factor and examined by confocal microscopy under a modified WHO classification, the endothelial/vascular pattern differed across tumor grades, with higher-grade tumors showing greater vessel density [PMID:9427037]. Control brain tissues showed a few, widely separated vessels [PMID:9427037]. Pilocytic astrocytomas (four cases) showed lacy clusters of small-to-medium sized vessels with intact vessel wall integrity [PMID:9427037]. Diffuse low grade astrocytoma (three cases) showed a staining pattern similar to control tissue, whereas intermediate grade (one case), anaplastic astrocytoma (three cases) and glioblastoma multiforme (six cases) showed increased vessel density with multiple small vessels forming glomeruloid clusters, some with prominent intimal hyperplasia, loss of vessel wall integrity, and numerous vWF-positive single cells/microvessels within the tumor substance [PMID:9427037]. Because this is a descriptive morphologic evaluation of surgical specimens with small case numbers in several grade categories (for example, one intermediate grade case), it supports an association between vascular pattern and grade rather than establishing the diagnostic accuracy of endothelial patterns for grading [PMID:9427037].
