planted_answer: In uveal melanoma, c-kit expression was found in 84 of 134 paraffin-embedded tumour samples by immunohistochemistry and in six of eight fresh-frozen samples by Western blot analysis [PMID:15223779]. c-Kit was weakly expressed and tyrosine phosphorylated in cultured uveal melanoma cells (OCM-1, OCM-3 and 92-1) compared with cutaneous melanoma cells, and in contrast to cutaneous melanoma cell lines it maintained a high phosphorylation level in serum-depleted uveal melanoma cells [PMID:15223779]. Expression of the stem cell growth factor (c-kit ligand) was detected in all three uveal melanoma cell lines, suggesting autocrine (paracrine) stimulation pathways, while no activation-related mutations were found in exon 11 of the KIT gene [PMID:15223779]. Treatment of uveal melanoma cell lines with STI571, which blocks c-kit autophosphorylation, resulted in cell death, and the IC(50) of the inhibitory effects on c-kit phosphorylation and on cell proliferation was of equal size and less than 2.5 microM, indicating that c-kit is a potential therapeutic target in uveal melanoma [PMID:15223779]. This therapeutic-target evidence derives from in vitro cell-line experiments, so the design does not establish that inhibiting c-kit improves clinical outcomes in patients with uveal melanoma [PMID:15223779].

planted_answer: The evidence is mixed: elderly and younger cancer patients differ in some care needs and treatment attitudes, but a cross-sectional survey of patients aged 35-82 (subgroups ≤65 vs ≥66 years) found few significant differences between the two age subgroups apart from issues such as the need for intimacy and support [PMID:21789019]. In that survey, the requests most frequently expressed by the older group were financial-insurance information (73.9%), the need to talk to people with the same illness (71.7%), the need for more comprehensible information from doctors and nurses (71.7%), and the need for better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%) [PMID:21789019]. Because this needs survey was an observational cross-sectional study, its age-related differences in expressed needs describe associations and cannot establish that changing care delivery by age would improve outcomes [PMID:21789019]. In a comparison of cohorts aged <65 years and 65+ years, disease diagnosis differed between the cohorts (P<0.001) while treatment modalities were similar (P = 0.82) [PMID:11371137]. There was no difference between the <65 and 65+ cohorts in the desire for surgery offering a chance of disease cure (P = 0.75), except that the elderly desired cure more when treatment was associated with disfigurement (P = 0.029) [PMID:11371137]. Issues of sexuality and femininity associated with gynecologic cancer and treatment were more important to younger patients (P<0.001), whereas the elderly supported equality of care with relation to age more strongly than the young and believed more strongly that doctors should make management decisions (P<0.001) [PMID:11371137]. Older patients with lung cancer are less likely to be offered surgery than younger patients, although the retrieved report does not provide the results of its comparison of symptom occurrence, severity, and distress between older (≥65 years) and younger (<65 years) patients prior to surgery [PMID:23916857]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: differences in symptom occurrence, severity, and distress between older and younger lung cancer patients prior to surgery.

planted_answer: A total of 80,565 Papanicolaou (Pap) smears underwent RPS during a 25-month period [PMID:26348845]. The final cytologic interpretation was a glandular cell abnormality (≥AGC) in 107 samples (0.13%); 39 of these (36.4%) were flagged as R on RPS [PMID:26348845]. Twenty-four patients (33.8%) out of 71 who had histologic follow-up were found to harbor a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or carcinoma; 13 of those 24 Pap smears (54.2%) had been flagged as R on RPS [PMID:26348845]. Notably, 11 AGC cases were picked up by RPS only and not by FS and represented false-negative cases; 2 of these showed endometrial adenocarcinoma on histologic follow-up [PMID:26348845]. The efficacy of RPS has been previously studied but exclusively with respect to squamous lesions; in fact, there has been no study so far specifically looking at the sensitivity of RPS for detecting glandular cell abnormalities [PMID:26348845].

planted_answer: Opioid dependence and methadone maintenance treatment (MMT) are documented in the medical record, but documentation is frequently missing: among 84 patients from a methadone clinic who received primary care at an affiliated but separate medical center, opioid dependence documentation was absent in 30% (95% CI, 20%-41%) and MMT documentation was absent from either the last primary care note or the last hospital discharge summary in 11% (95% CI, 5%-19%) [PMID:19578820]. Electronic medical records of those patients were reviewed for documentation of methadone, opioid dependence, and potential drug-methadone interactions, and the proportions of records containing opioid dependence and methadone documentation were then estimated [PMID:19578820]. The study was designed to identify potential safety risks among MMT patients engaged in medical care by evaluating how often opioid dependence and MMT documentation are missing from medical records and by characterizing potential medication-methadone interactions [PMID:19578820].

original: Yes — in a retrospective review of 241 patients with acetabular fractures treated through a posterior approach and followed radiographically for at least 6 months, surrogates of injury severity were significantly associated with the development of heterotopic ossification (HO) in a multivariate model: ICU length of stay (LOS) of 1-2 days had an odds ratio (OR) of 4.33 (95% CI 1.03-18.25), 3-6 days an OR of 4.1 (95% CI 1.27-13.27), and >6 days an OR of 11.7 (95% CI 3.24-42.22) [PMID:26606599].

planted_answer: Yes — in a retrospective review of 214 patients with acetabular fractures treated through a posterior approach and followed radiographically for at least 6 months, surrogates of injury severity were significantly associated with the development of heterotopic ossification (HO) in a multivariate model: ICU length of stay (LOS) of 1-2 days had an odds ratio (OR) of 4.33 (95% CI 1.03-18.25), 3-6 days an OR of 4.1 (95% CI 1.27-13.27), and >6 days an OR of 11.7 (95% CI 3.24-42.22) [PMID:26606599]. In the same multivariate model, non-ICU LOS >10 days versus 0-6 days was associated with HO development (OR = 7.6, 95% CI 2.6-22.25), while HO prophylaxis with external radiation beam therapy (XRT) was associated with lower odds of HO (OR = 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.85) [PMID:26606599]. Other variables evaluated in the multivariate modeling that were not significantly associated with either the development or the severity of HO included age, gender, mechanism of injury, injury severity score, presence of neurologic injury, Letournel fracture type, occurrence of hip dislocation, interval from injury to surgery, operative time, and estimated blood loss [PMID:26606599].

planted_answer: The cited evidence is mixed: the automated GAPS score was comparable to triage nurses' visual analogue scale (VAS) estimate of admission probability across the whole cohort, but in the majority of attendances where nurses were less than 95% certain, GAPS significantly outperformed the nurses, and a combined strategy was best [PMID:26864326]. In this single-centre prospective study of 1829 attendances, 745 (40.7%) were admitted, not significantly different from GAPS' prediction of 750 (41.0%, p=0.678), whereas the nurses' mean VAS predicted 865 admissions (47.3%), an overestimate of 6.6% (p<0.0001) [PMID:26864326]. Over the whole cohort, GAPS proved capable of determining whether patients should be admitted or discharged as well as the nurses, with an AUC of 0.876 versus 0.875 for VAS (p=0.93), and as a binary predictor its accuracy was 80.6%, comparable with VAS at 79.0% (p=0.18) [PMID:26864326]. In the minority of attendances where nurses felt at least 95% certain of the outcome, VAS accuracy was excellent at 92.4% [PMID:26864326]. In the remaining majority of attendances, GAPS significantly outperformed VAS on calibration (+1.2% vs +9.2%, p<0.0001), discrimination (AUC 0.810 vs 0.759, p=0.001) and accuracy (75.1% vs 68.9%, p=0.0009) [PMID:26864326]. Using GAPS but over-ruling it when clinical certainty was at least 95% significantly outperformed either method alone, with AUC 0.891 (0.877-0.907) and accuracy 82.5% (80.7%-84.2%) [PMID:26864326]. Interpretation is limited by the design: the comparison comes from a single-centre prospective study in which nurses estimated admission probability using a 100 mm VAS while GAPS was generated automatically from triage data, so the head-to-head performance figures describe that one centre's cohort [PMID:26864326].

planted_answer: This study provides the first large-volume (1000 implant) comparison of the deflation rates of Poly Implant Prosthesis prefilled textured saline breast implants versus a control group of Mentor Siltex textured saline implants; a consecutive series of 500 Poly Implant Prosthesis prefilled textured saline breast implants was compared with a consecutive series of 500 Mentor Siltex breast implants, and each breast implant was evaluated for a 4-year period [PMID:16772913]. The cumulative deflation rates of the Poly Implant Prosthesis implants were: year 1, 1.2 percent; year 2, 5.6 percent; year 3, 11.4 percent; and year 4, 15.4 percent. The cumulative deflation rates of the Allergan implants were: year 1, 0.2 percent; year 2, 0.6 percent; year 3, 1.6 percent; and year 4, 4.4 percent [PMID:16772913]. Because the study compared two consecutive series rather than randomly assigning implants, the observed difference in deflation rates represents an association and does not establish the effect of intervening on the exposure (i.e., choosing one implant type over the other) [PMID:16772913]. Statistical significance was calculated with Fisher's exact test at year 1 and chi-square analysis at years 2 through 4; the difference in deflation rates was not statistically significant at year 1 (Fisher's exact test, p>0.05), but was statistically significant at year 2 (chi-square, 13.29; p<0.001), year 3 (chi-square, 37.91; p<0.001) and year 4 (chi-square, 32.69; p<0.001) [PMID:16772913].

planted_answer: The cited evidence indicates that prostate specific antigen does not need to be adjusted for body mass index: in 994 men (4,937 observations) without prostate cancer in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, body mass index was not significantly associated with prostate specific antigen after adjusting for age (p = 0.06), and a 10-point body mass index increase corresponded to a prostate specific antigen difference of only -0.03 ng/ml (95% CI -0.40-0.49) [PMID:19836806]. In the same longitudinal aging study, results were similar when men with prostate cancer were included, when percent body fat was substituted for body mass index, and after adjusting for prostate volume, and longitudinal weight changes also did not affect prostate specific antigen; separate models explored men with prostate cancer censored at diagnosis, percent body fat measurements, weight changes with time, and adjustment for initial prostate size in 483 men (2,523 observations) with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging measurements [PMID:19836806]. In a separate cohort of 6,103 men who had a 2-year biopsy, of whom 1,646 (27%) were normal weight, 3,209 (53%) overweight and 1,248 (20%) obese, mean adjusted prostate specific antigen for normal weight, overweight and obese subjects was 7.73, 7.17 and 6.79 ng/ml on placebo (p-trend = 0.192) and 3.16, 2.93 and 2.62 ng/ml on dutasteride (p = 0.008) [PMID:25661298]. In that study, AUC analysis using raw prostate specific antigen data for predicting prostate cancer ranged from 0.60 to 0.64 in the placebo arm and 0.58 to 0.66 in the dutasteride arm with no difference across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.212), and similar results were found for high grade prostate cancer with AUC ranging from 0.69 to 0.70 in the placebo arm and 0.65 to 0.75 in the dutasteride arm but no differences across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.157) [PMID:25661298].
